title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Iterative radix-2 divider (off the EX critical path) + single 33x33 signed multiplier
motivation:
The baseline Fmax is 5.442 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) runs
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex, which is the forwarding mux
feeding the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` operators in alu.sv
(DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU each become a ~32-level ripple-subtract array).
Those dividers also account for most of the 12.3k LUT4s. Nothing else in the
5-stage pipeline is anywhere near 200 ns: add, compare, shift, the
branch-to-PC redirect and the load-align paths are all around 10-20 ns on
GW2A. CoreMark -O3 runs almost no divides inside the timed region
(list/matrix/state/crc use MUL, add, shift and compare), so making divide
multi-cycle costs practically no IPC and removes a path that is about 10x
longer than the next one. The multiplier is the next-worst unit: alu.sv
builds three separate 64-bit products (ss, uu, su), which triples the
DSP/LUT cost and widens the output mux.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU out of the combinational ALU and run them in a small
sequential divider (new rtl/divider.sv) instantiated in ex_stage. Also
replace the three 64-bit multipliers with one 33x33 signed multiply.

Divider (restoring radix-2, one quotient bit per cycle):
  * START (EX holds a valid DIV* op, divider idle and not done): latch the
    post-forward rs1/rs2 (the forwarding mux output feeds only flops), the op
    and the sign bits. Take |a| and |b| in the first busy cycle, not in the
    forwarding cycle.
  * RUN: 32 iterations of the 33-bit trial subtract plus shift-in of the
    {rem, quo} pair. Each iteration is one ~33-bit carry chain plus a mux,
    well under 15 ns.
  * FIX: one registered cycle for the sign fix-up (negate the quotient if
    the signs differ, negate the remainder if the dividend was negative) and
    the RV32M special case of divide-by-zero (q = all ones, r = dividend).
    INT_MIN / -1 comes out correct from the magnitude algorithm
    (q = 0x80000000, r = 0), but keep an explicit check anyway. The result
    goes into a flop, so no negate or special-case mux sits in the
    EX -> EX/MEM path.
  * DONE: result_q is valid and div_busy = 0. EX/MEM captures result_q in
    place of the ALU output on the first cycle it is not held by the dmem
    stall (stall_ex_mem). The divider then goes back to IDLE. If
    stall_ex_mem is high it stays in DONE.
  Total latency is about 34 cycles per divide. Early-out is not needed.

Pipeline integration (reuses the existing freeze machinery):
  * div_busy = id_ex.valid && is_div_op && !done. It comes only from flops,
    so its fan-out is cheap.
  * hazard_unit: stall_if |= div_busy; stall_id |= div_busy with NO flush,
    so ID/EX holds the divide and the PC holds, just like the dmem-stall
    hold path.
  * ex_stage: while div_busy, EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0,
    reg_write=0, mem_read=0, mem_write=0, is_jump=0). Older instructions in
    MEM and WB drain normally. dmem stall (stall_ex_mem) keeps priority and
    holds EX/MEM.
  * RVFI correctness: the older producers drain while the divide waits, so
    the forwarding mux (and the stale ID/EX rs?_val) can no longer supply
    the operand values used at START. When the divide retires, EX/MEM's
    rs1_val/rs2_val/write_data must come from the divider's latched
    operands, not from the live forward mux. Otherwise rvfi_rs1_rdata and
    rvfi_rs2_rdata are wrong and the reg/insn formal checks fail.
  * A divide in EX can never be squashed: redirects come from EX itself,
    and there are no exceptions from MEM/WB. So only reset needs to clear
    the FSM.

Formal (ALTOPS) contract: checks_si.cfg's liveness check requires the next
instruction to retire within about 10 cycles of the trigger, so a 34-cycle
divide would break it under formal. Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the
divider keeps the same FSM and handshake with a short iteration count (for
example 2 RUN cycles). Its result is the existing ALTOPS formula
((a - b) ^ const per op) applied to the latched operands. Formal still
checks the busy/stall/bubble/operand-capture logic, and liveness stays
within the window. The real iterative datapath is covered by test_alu.py
vectors, cosim against reference.py (every retired DIV/REM is diffed) and
formal-deep.

Multiplier: build one product
prod = $signed({sa & a[31], a}) * $signed({sb & b[31], b}) (66 bits), with
sa = (op is MULH or MULHSU) and sb = (op is MULH). MUL takes prod[31:0] and
MULH/MULHSU/MULHU take prod[63:32]. Gowin maps a single signed 33x33
product onto its DSP MULT36X36 or MULT18X18 cascade, instead of three
64-bit products plus a 4-way mux. This cuts DSP and LUT use and makes the
next-critical EX path (forward mux -> multiply -> EX/MEM) shorter. The ALTOPS
branch for MUL* is unchanged.

Expected result: with the divider gone, the EX path becomes
forward mux -> 33x33 DSP multiply -> result mux -> EX/MEM, roughly
20-30 ns. Fmax should go from 5.4 MHz to about 35-50 MHz. IPC stays within
about 1% of baseline because CoreMark rarely divides, and LUT4 drops by
several thousand. The real fitness gain is expected to be several hundred
percent. It is capped at +50 below only because of the schema range.

changes.description: New module. Ports: clock, reset, start, op, a, b, advance (= !stall_ex_mem), busy, result, a_latched, b_latched. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS it uses a short iteration count and outputs the ALTOPS (a-b)^const formula on the latched operands, so formal liveness still fits in the 10-cycle window.

Replace the three 64-bit products with one signed 33x33 product whose operand sign-extension is chosen per op (MULH: both signed; MULHSU: a signed; MULHU/MUL: unsigned).

title: Move MUL/DIV out of the single-cycle EX ALU into a multi-cycle M-unit with EX stall
motivation:
The baseline's Fmax is 5.44 MHz: the worst path (199.8 ns, 150 logic levels,
156 cells) runs MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> EX operand mux -> u_alu -> the
dmem BSRAM address. The cause is that alu.sv evaluates a fully combinational
32-bit signed/unsigned DIVIDER (`/`, `%`) and three 64-bit multipliers
(mul_ss / mul_uu / mul_su, which use 6 DSPs) in the same cycle as ADD/SUB. The
divider is an array of about 32 cascaded 32-bit subtract/select rows, and it
sets the clock for every instruction, even though DIV/REM are a very small
share of CoreMark's dynamic instruction mix and MUL is only a few percent.
A plain 5-stage RV32I datapath on GW2A-18 (a forwarding mux, a 32-bit
add/shift/compare and a branch redirect) should close timing far above
40 MHz. Removing the arithmetic array from the single-cycle path should
therefore raise Fmax by about 8-12x, while CPI (cycles per instruction) rises
by only a few percent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove all eight M-extension ops from the combinational `alu` and execute
them in a new sequential unit, `rtl/muldiv.sv`. The unit sits beside the ALU
in EX and uses a start/busy/done handshake. The pipeline holds IF, ID and
ID/EX, and puts a bubble into EX/MEM, until the result is ready.

muldiv.sv (new):
  * Operand latch. When a valid M-op is in ID/EX and the unit is idle, it
    latches the POST-FORWARDING rs1/rs2 values (the EX `rs1`/`rs2` mux
    outputs). The latch is needed because the stall lasts several cycles:
    the producer ahead of the M-op drains out of EX/MEM and MEM/WB, so the
    forwarding source disappears and ID/EX.rs?_val would then be stale. The
    latched copies also feed EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val on the completion cycle,
    so the RVFI rs?_rdata fields stay correct.
  * Multiplier. One signed 33x33 multiply,
    {sa&a[31],a} * {sb&b[31],b}, where sa/sb come from MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU.
    This single multiplier replaces the three separate 64-bit products.
    Operands are registered, the product is registered (so Gowin can absorb
    both register stages into the MULT36X36/MULT18X18 DSP registers), and
    [31:0] or [63:32] is selected. MUL* has a latency of 3 EX cycles, i.e.
    2 stall cycles.
  * Divider. A radix-2 restoring divider on |a| and |b|: one setup cycle,
    32 iterations of a 33-bit subtract with shift, then one sign-fix cycle
    (negate the quotient if sign(a)^sign(b), negate the remainder if
    sign(a)). The worst case is about 34 cycles. The RV32M special cases are
    handled explicitly: divide by zero gives quotient 0xFFFFFFFF and
    remainder = dividend, and the quotient sign-fix is suppressed when b==0.
    The overflow case INT_MIN/-1 falls out naturally
    (|INT_MIN| = 0x80000000, the negation wraps back, and the remainder is 0).
    Optional early-out: when b==0, skip the iterations.
  * Done/hold behaviour. When the result is ready the unit asserts `done`
    and holds the result until EX/MEM actually captures it. Capture happens
    when !stall_ex_mem, so a concurrent dmem stall on the instruction ahead
    is handled correctly. After capture the unit returns to IDLE, which
    prevents it from restarting on the same instruction.
  * ALTOPS. Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the unit keeps the same
    latch/busy/done FSM but returns the riscv-formal ALTOPS formulas (moved
    verbatim from alu.sv) computed from the latched operands. It uses a
    short fixed latency of 2 EX cycles for every M-op. The whole
    stall/operand-latch/RVFI-capture path is therefore still proven by the
    insn/reg/pc/causal/unique/liveness checks inside the depth-20 BMC
    window. A 34-cycle divide could not retire inside the 10-cycle liveness
    window. The real (non-ALTOPS) latency is only a count constant; all
    handshake logic is shared by both builds.

alu.sv: delete the mul_* products and the DIV/REM arms, including the
ALTOPS M arms, which move to muldiv.sv. ALU_* encodings stay in core_pkg.sv.
Add an `is_muldiv` bit to ctrl_t, or derive it as alu_op >= ALU_MUL.

ex_stage.sv: instantiate muldiv. Output `md_busy` = in.valid && is_muldiv &&
!md_done. When the M-op completes, write md_result into
EX/MEM.alu_result. While md_busy && !stall, write a bubble into EX/MEM:
valid=0, and ctrl.reg_write/mem_read/mem_write/is_branch/is_jump all 0, so
neither forwarding nor the dmem port sees a phantom op.

hazard_unit.sv: add an `md_busy` input. Set stall_if and stall_id when
md_busy. Do NOT set flush_id for md_busy, so ID/EX holds the M-op. The
priority order is dmem_stall (hold everything), then md_busy (freeze the
front end and bubble EX/MEM), then load-use and redirect. load_use must not
flush ID/EX while md_busy, because the M-op, not a load, occupies ID/EX.
Redirect cannot coincide with md_busy because an M-op is never a branch.

The expected result is Fmax going from 5.4 MHz to at least 45 MHz; the new
critical path should be the forward -> ALU add/compare -> redirect -> PC,
or -> dmem-address, path. CoreMark cycles rise by about 3-8% (MUL
+2 cycles each; DIV/REM +33 but rare). Net fitness should rise by far more
than the 4.6% acceptance bar (the schema caps the reported delta at +50).
LUT4 use should also fall sharply from 12.3k, because the combinational
divider array is most of the current LUT count.

changes.description: New sequential M-extension unit: latches post-forwarding operands, computes MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU with one registered signed 33x33 (DSP) product in 3 cycles, and DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU with a radix-2 restoring divider (about 34 cycles) that handles div-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 explicitly. It has a start/busy/done handshake and holds the result until the EX/MEM capture. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS it returns the ALTOPS formulas after a fixed 2-cycle latency through the same FSM.
Remove the mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su products and all eight M-extension case arms, including the ALTOPS arms, which move to muldiv.sv. The ALU keeps only single-cycle RV32I ops.
Add an is_muldiv control bit to ctrl_t (or a helper localparam range check), and extend ex_mem_t only if needed. ALU_* encodings stay unchanged.
Set is_muldiv=1 in the funct7=0000001 R-type arm. Legality logic is untouched: is_illegal still defaults to 1 and is cleared only in validated arms.

Instantiate muldiv and feed it the forwarded rs1/rs2. Export md_busy. On completion, select md_result into EX/MEM.alu_result and use the latched operands for EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val/write_data. Add an md_busy input. It holds the PC and ID/EX (stall_if and stall_id without flush_id), and gets priority below dmem_stall and above load-use/redirect.
Wire md_busy from ex_stage to hazard_unit. The RVFI mapping is otherwise unchanged.
Keep all RV32I vectors against the combinational alu. Move the M-ext vectors out to test_muldiv.py; none are deleted.

New clocked cocotb suite for muldiv.sv. It contains every M-ext vector formerly in test_alu.py (MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU, DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU, div-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1 overflow, back-to-back divides) plus a few hundred random vectors checked against Python reference semantics. It drives start, waits for done, and checks that the result holds while capture is withheld.

Add a pipeline-level test of the stall and forwarding corners the multi-cycle unit creates. The program is: ADDI x1 -> MUL x2,x1,x1, where the operand comes by forwarding from EX/MEM and must be latched before the producer drains. Next comes LW x3 -> DIV x4,x3,x2, a load-use case followed by a long stall. Then ADD x5,x4,x2, which consumes the M result through EX/MEM forwarding, and back-to-back MULHU/REMU. title: Zero-bubble IF-stage next-PC prediction: predecode JAL + BTFN-seeded 64-entry bimodal BHT
motivation:
This core fetches and decodes in the same cycle (there is no IF/ID flop:
io_imemData is decoded combinationally and captured straight into ID/EX).
Every taken branch and every JAL/JALR is resolved only in EX, so each one
costs exactly one bubble: the pc+4 instruction fetched while the transfer
sits in EX is squashed (flush_if = redirect) and the target is fetched a
cycle late.

Measured on the reference ISS over the timed CoreMark window (2K,
-O3, ITERATIONS=10, between the 0x10000100/0x10000104 markers):
  instructions            2,922,015   (baseline ~4.49M cycles, CPI ~1.54)
  conditional branches      529,588   (294,425 taken = 55.6%)
    backward                287,132   (235,191 taken)
  JAL                        49,367
  JALR (all are `ret`)       13,735
=> 357,527 taken control transfers = 357k redirect bubbles = ~8% of all
cycles. Fmax is pinned at ~5.4 MHz by the combinational divider (199.8 ns
path fwd -> ALU), so extra next-PC logic in IF is far off the critical
path: cycles saved convert ~1:1 into fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Since the instruction word is available in IF in the same cycle its PC is
presented, the target of JAL and of conditional branches can be computed
in IF (pc + J/B immediate taken directly from io_imemData) and loaded into
the PC register at the end of the fetch cycle. A correctly predicted taken
transfer then costs ZERO bubbles instead of one; only mispredicts pay the
existing 1-cycle EX redirect.

Direction predictor (simulated on the same trace):
  static BTFN only            111,175 mispredicts (21.0%)
  64-entry bimodal, BTFN-seeded 46,325 mispredicts ( 8.7%)
  256-entry bimodal, BTFN-seeded 39,609 (7.5%) - not worth the area
Net cycles saved with 64 entries: (294,425 - 46,325) branch bubbles
+ 49,367 JAL bubbles = ~297k of ~4.49M cycles = -6.6% cycles
=> ~+7% fitness at unchanged Fmax. JALR/ret (13.7k) left as-is.

Mechanism:
1. if_stage.sv: predecode imem_data (opcode==JAL / opcode==BRANCH with a
   legal funct3), build the J- or B-immediate, one adder pc + imm.
   pred_taken = imem_ready && !stall && !redirect && imm[1]==0 &&
                (is_jal || (is_branch && bht_predict)).
   imm[1]==0 guard: never predict a misaligned target; EX's existing
   misalign trap (no redirect, pc_next = pc+4) stays untouched.
   PC update priority: reset > EX redirect > stall hold >
   pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. The predicted instruction itself is
   valid and is NOT flushed - only the next PC changes.
2. BHT: 64 x 2-bit table indexed by pc[7:2], read combinationally from
   the PC register (in parallel with the imem access, no dependence on
   imem_data). Counters are stored in "disagree with BTFN" form:
   bht_predict = imm_sign(instr[31]) XOR counter[1]; reset all entries
   to 2'b01 (weakly agree, as simulated) so cold branches behave as
   backward-taken/forward-not-taken and the table only learns
   exceptions. Update once per resolved conditional branch in EX:
   en = id_ex.valid && is_branch && !stall_ex_mem, index = id_ex.pc[7:2],
   disagree = (branch_taken != instr[31]) -> saturating inc, else dec.
3. core_pkg.sv / id_stage.sv: add pred_taken to if_id_t and id_ex_t
   (flush/bubble clears it).
4. ex_stage.sv: redirect only on mispredict (still gated by
   !misalign_fault):
     branch: redirect = (branch_taken != pred_taken),
             target   = branch_taken ? pc+imm : pc+4
     JAL   : redirect = !pred_taken
     JALR  : redirect = 1 (unchanged)
   pc_next / all RVFI fields remain the architectural next PC, so
   riscv-formal (pc_fwd/pc_bwd, liveness) and cosim are unaffected.
Wrong-path safety: the only instruction younger than EX is the one in IF,
and it is squashed (and its prediction suppressed via the !redirect gate)
in the same cycle as any EX redirect, so the predictor never acts on a
wrong-path instruction and needs no recovery state. While a branch is
held in EX by a dmem stall its redirect re-fires idempotently (as today)
and the BHT trains only on the releasing cycle.

title: Co-trim the two tied EX critical paths: redirect off the IF/hazard cone + registered fwd hits and dedicated AGU into dmem
motivation:
The champion (47.3 MHz) has two nearly tied ~26.6-26.9 ns paths, so
fixing only one of them gains nothing. That is measured here, not
guessed: in this hypgen session I applied only the redirect-decoupling
part (items 1-3 below) and ran `make timing TARGET=bench`. Logic levels
fell from 23 to 16, but Fmax stayed at 47.0 MHz because the next path
is right behind:
  cpu/u_mem/reg_q.rd (MEM/WB.rd) -> u_fwd 5-bit rd==rs compare
  -> u_ex 3:1 forward mux -> u_alu adder -> ALU op-select mux
  -> ex_stage result mux (div_done / is_jump) -> EX/MEM.alu_result,
  which Gowin absorbs as the dmem BSRAM address register (endpoint
  dmem_N_dmem_N_0_0_s, 26.57 ns, 18 cells).
The original worst path (regfile BSRAM -> fwd mux -> branch compare ->
redirect -> IF NOP mux -> hazard load-use -> stall -> PC/ID-EX enables)
must be cut too. Both paths start with the forwarding compare and
mux in EX, and both have logic that is not needed in that cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Timing-only micro-optimisations. CoreMark cycle count stays identical
(~4.49M); only Fmax moves.
A. Redirect off the IF/hazard cone (verified to take the old worst
   path from 23 to 16 levels):
   1. if_stage: out.instr = imem_data always (drop the NOP mux); only
      out.valid = !(flush || redirect) carries the kill.
   2. core/hazard_unit: load-use uses raw io_imemData[19:15]/[24:20].
      This gives the same behaviour: redirect implies ID/EX holds a
      branch/jump, so id_ex_mem_read=0 and load_use=0 anyway. During
      an imem stall, a spurious load_use from garbage bits only raises
      stall_if (already high) and bubbles ID/EX (which gets a bubble
      anyway).
   3. id_stage: ID/EX sync-clears when reset || flush || (!stall &&
      !in.valid). Garbage fetch words then never reach EX with live
      ctrl bits.
B. Registered forwarding hits (removes the u_fwd 5-bit compares from
   the start of every EX path). When ID captures instruction X, which
   requires !dmem_stall && !load_use && !div_busy, EX/MEM will next hold
   the current ID/EX instruction and MEM/WB the current EX/MEM
   instruction. So register in ID/EX:
     hit1_ex  = id_ex.rd != 0 && id_ex.rd == X.rs1   (same for rs2)
     hit1_mem = ex_mem.rd != 0 && ex_mem.rd == X.rs1 (same for rs2)
   In EX, qualify with the live registered write enables so that
   misalign traps, which clear reg_write, stay exact:
     sel = (hit_ex && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write) ? EX_MEM
         : (hit_mem && mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write) ? MEM_WB : ID_EX value.
   Stall cases stay correct. Under dmem_stall, ID/EX, EX/MEM and the
   MEM/WB data (rd and reg_write kept by hold_wb) all freeze. Under
   div_busy the divider latches its operands in the first EX cycle,
   when the hits are fresh. Load-use and redirect insert bubbles, so
   their operand values are don't-care. Keep forward_unit only if still
   needed, or delete it.
C. Dedicated AGU for the dmem address: in EX compute
   mem_addr = fwd_rs1 + imm with its own adder (no ALU op mux, no
   div/jump result mux). Register it in a new ex_mem.mem_addr field
   that drives io_dmemAddr, the byte-mask/misalign logic and the RVFI
   mem_addr. alu_result keeps feeding forwarding and WB. Only
   LOAD/STORE use the address, so the ALU result mux is off the BSRAM
   address path.
Then the EX paths are: registered hit -> 2-level mux -> 32-bit carry
chain -> BSRAM/flop (AGU), and fwd mux -> compare -> redirect ->
{PC D-mux, ID/EX sync-clear}. That is about 5-7 fewer LUT levels on
each of the two tied paths. Expected Fmax is about 47 -> 53-56 MHz.

title: 4-stage IF/ID-EX-MEM(+WB) pipeline: drop MEM/WB, 2:1 EX bypass with ID-registered select, flop-only stall control
motivation:
The champion (hyp-20260929-001-r1s0) runs at 47.3 MHz, far below the 135 MHz
target. Its worst path is 26.9 ns over 23 logic levels:
regfile BSRAM -> u_id -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id -> u_if/pc. Three
things in the 5-stage topology put that chain in one cycle:
  1. The EX operand network is a 3:1 bypass (ID/EX value, EX/MEM alu_result,
     MEM/WB wb_w_data). Its select comes from forward_unit's 5-bit rd/rs
     compares on the same edge, so the compare -> select -> mux sits in front
     of both the ALU and the branch comparator.
  2. The EX branch decision (redirect) forces the fetched word to a NOP in
     if_stage. That NOP word feeds hazard_unit's load-use compare, which
     drives stall_if/stall_id, the PC enable and the ID/EX enable. So the
     branch compare is chained with a second compare and a high-fanout
     enable.
  3. flush_id resets every ID/EX flop (about 200), so redirect carries a
     very large fanout.
The MEM/WB stage only exists so WB can write the regfile one cycle after
MEM. Its cost is the third bypass source, the hold_mem_wb "valid-only
clear" special case, and roughly 400 extra flops. Most of those flops feed
only RVFI.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change the pipeline to four stages: IF/ID (combinational fetch plus decode,
as today) -> EX -> MEM. MEM also does writeback: it writes the regfile
directly at the end of the MEM cycle. After that, every control signal on
the EX critical loop comes straight from a flop.

A) Remove the MEM/WB register (structural).
   * Regfile write port, driven from MEM combinationally:
     w_en = ex_mem.valid && reg_write && !mem_misalign && !dmem_stall
     w_addr = ex_mem.rd
     w_data = mem_to_reg ? load_data : ex_mem.alu_result
     The write-first bypass already in reg_file.sv covers producers at
     distance 2: the producer is in MEM while the consumer reads in ID.
   * Retirement and RVFI move to the MEM stage:
     rvfi_valid = ex_mem.valid && !dmem_stall
     RVFI fields come from the EX/MEM register plus MEM combinational values
     (load_data, dmem_rdata, masks, aligned address). rvfi_order increments
     on that same condition. RVFI is untimed, so it may be combinational.
   * Remove hold_mem_wb and the valid-only-clear special case. dmem_stall
     still freezes PC, ID/EX and EX/MEM. The stalled load writes the
     regfile in the cycle the bus delivers.
   * Load-use keeps its single bubble. With the bubble, the consumer sits in
     ID while the load is in MEM, so the loaded value arrives through the
     regfile write-first bypass into ID/EX. The IPC is identical to today's.

B) Collapse the EX bypass to a 2:1 mux with a select registered in ID.
   * In ID, compute
     fwd1_d = id_ex.valid && id_ex.ctrl.reg_write && id_ex.rd != 0
              && id_ex.rd == rs1_addr
     and fwd2_d the same way for rs2. The instruction in ID/EX becomes the
     EX/MEM occupant exactly when ID/EX captures (stall_id = 0 means no
     dmem stall and no div_busy). Load producers never set it, because
     load-use stalls the consumer.
   * Register fwd1_q/fwd2_q in ID/EX. In EX:
     rs1 = fwd1_q ? ex_mem.alu_result : id_ex.rs1_val (rs2 likewise).
     Delete forward_unit.sv and the fwd_mem_wb input.
   * Under a dmem stall EX/MEM holds its producer, so the select stays
     valid. A DIV latches its operands on its first non-stalled EX cycle,
     while the producer is still in EX/MEM. After that, EX/MEM bubbles make
     the stale select harmless. Keep that ordering.
   * Keep the 33x33 DSP MUL single-cycle in EX (LESSONS: a stalling
     multi-cycle MUL lost IPC).

C) Make stall and flush control depend only on flops, and give redirect a
   small fanout.
   * hazard_unit's load-use check reads the raw fetched word's
     instr[19:15] and [24:20] (io_imemData), not the NOP-muxed IF payload.
     Load-use (a LOAD in EX) and redirect (a branch/jump in EX) are
     mutually exclusive. On an imem stall a spurious load-use gives the
     same bubble. So stall_if and stall_id no longer depend on redirect.
   * Redirect no longer resets all of ID/EX. It only clears
     ID/EX.valid and the side-effect bits (reg_write, mem_read, mem_write,
     is_branch, is_jump, fwd*_q), with valid = imem_ready && !redirect
     gating those bits in ID. The data fields keep capturing freely. Drop
     the NOP-instruction mux in if_stage. Decode sees the raw word and
     validity rides on the valid bit.
   * The PC mux stays redirect ? target : (stall_if ? pc : pc + 4), with
     redirect keeping its priority.

Expected effect: the remaining EX loop is ID/EX flop -> 2:1 mux (select is
a flop) -> ALU or branch compare -> result mux or PC mux / valid clear. That
removes about 8-10 of the 23 levels and all high-fanout stall/flush
coupling from the redirect path. The estimate is Fmax 47 -> 62-70 MHz with
unchanged cycles per iteration (same load-use and branch penalties),
about +30% fitness. Risk: once the control chain is gone, the next limit is
probably the DSP multiply or the dmem BSRAM -> load-align -> regfile/bypass
path. Both have a lot of headroom compared to 26.9 ns.

title: IF-stage BTFN-seeded bimodal predictor with a registered (off-critical-path) mispredict redirect
motivation:
The champion (hyp-20260929-001-r1s0, 47.3 MHz, 105.38) is limited by the
EX -> IF redirect chain. Its worst path (26.9 ns, 23 logic levels) runs
regfile/ID-EX -> u_ex (forward mux, 32-bit branch compare) -> u_if
(redirect -> NOP-instruction mux) -> u_hazard (load-use compare on the
now-NOP'd rs1/rs2 -> stall_if) -> u_id -> u_if (PC enable). Every
taken branch, JAL and JALR costs one bubble because it is only resolved
in EX. The ISS trace of the timed CoreMark window shows 2.92M
instructions, 294k taken conditional branches, 49k JAL and 13.7k JALR,
so about 357k redirect bubbles out of 4.49M cycles (~8%).

hyp-20260929-003-r1s2 showed that a same-cycle IF predecode plus a
64-entry BTFN-seeded bimodal BHT gives the IPC gain the trace predicts
(+6.44% measured vs +7% estimated). But it kept a combinational
mispredict redirect from EX into the PC, so on the fast base it would
add more logic to the path that is already critical. In the timed
FPGA harness, io_imemData comes straight from a flop (the LFSR in
fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so predecoding in IF is cheap: flop ->
opcode/imm decode -> pc+imm adder -> PC mux.

With a predictor that is right about 91% of the time, redirects become
rare. That makes it worth taking one extra bubble on a mispredict to
take the whole EX -> IF/hazard/PC combinational chain off the clock
period.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add zero-bubble next-PC prediction in IF and move mispredict recovery
onto a registered redirect. This improves IPC and Fmax together.

1. IF prediction (if_stage.sv). Predecode imem_data in the fetch cycle:
   is_jal (opcode 1101111) and is_br (opcode 1100011 with a legal
   funct3). Pick the J- or B-immediate from the instruction bits and
   compute a single adder, pc + imm.
   BHT: 64 x 2-bit counters indexed by pc[7:2] and read from the PC
   register, in parallel with the fetch. Counters are stored in
   "disagree with BTFN" form: predict = instr[31] XOR ctr[1]. Reset all
   counters to 2'b01, so a cold branch predicts backward-taken,
   forward-not-taken.
   pred_taken = valid fetch && !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_br && predict)).
   The !imm[1] term means a misaligned target is never predicted, so
   EX's existing misalign trap (no redirect, pc_next = pc+4) still
   works unchanged.
   PC priority: reset > redirect_q ? target_q : (stall ? hold :
   (pred_taken ? pc+imm : pc+4)).
   IF also sends pred_taken and alt_pc down the pipe. alt_pc is the PC
   that was not chosen: pc+4 if predicted taken, pc+imm if predicted
   not-taken.

2. EX resolution (ex_stage.sv). Compute:
     mispredict = valid && !kill && !misalign_fault &&
                  ((is_branch && branch_cond != pred_taken) ||
                   (is_jump && !is_jalr && !pred_taken) || is_jalr)
     fix_target = is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],0} : alt_pc
   These are NOT sent combinationally to IF. They are registered:
     redirect_q <= mispredict && !stall_ex_mem && !redirect_q
     target_q   <= fix_target
   A dmem-held branch registers its redirect only on the cycle it
   actually leaves EX. No adder sits between EX and the redirect flops
   except the JALR rs1+imm adder, because alt_pc is carried in from IF.
   The architectural pc_next and branch_target that feed RVFI stay
   exactly as they are today. Train the BHT from EX: a valid, un-killed
   conditional branch that is leaving EX (!stall_ex_mem) does a
   saturating update of the disagree counter with (taken XOR instr[31]).
   The update port may be registered one cycle if that is better for
   timing.

3. Recovery with a 2-bubble mispredict penalty (was 1 bubble for every
   taken transfer). On the cycle after a mispredict, redirect_q is 1:
     - PC <= target_q. This has priority over every stall.
     - The IF instruction becomes a NOP (flush_if |= redirect_q).
     - ID/EX captures a bubble even if dmem_stall is active
       (flush_id = redirect_q || (load_use && !dmem_stall)).
     - The wrong-path instruction now sitting in ID/EX is killed in EX
       (kill = redirect_q). EX/MEM captures a bubble with valid,
       reg_write, mem_read, mem_write and is_jump cleared, the divider
       start is gated, div_busy is forced to 0, it cannot mispredict,
       and it does not train the BHT.
   redirect_q, imem_ready and dmem_ready are all flop outputs, so the
   flush/hazard/PC-enable cone no longer depends on the EX comparator.

Cycle accounting from the r1s2 trace (64-entry bimodal: 46.3k
conditional-branch mispredicts):
  bubbles today : 294k + 49k + 13.7k        = ~357k
  bubbles after : 2 x (46.3k + 13.7k JALR)  = ~120k
That saves ~237k of 4.49M cycles (-5.3% cycles, +5.6% IPC).

Fmax: this removes the 26.9 ns redirect -> NOP mux -> load-use ->
stall -> PC chain. The paths left are EX -> EX/MEM (forward mux + ALU
or DSP multiply) and EX -> redirect_q/target_q (forward mux + compare
+ XOR, and forward mux + JALR adder). The new IF path is flop ->
predecode/BHT mux -> 32-bit adder -> PC mux, about the same as the
existing pc+4 / redirect-target mux. A conservative guess is 47 ->
52-56 MHz.
Combined expectation: +12% to +20% fitness.

title: Take the regfile out of BSRAM: distributed-RAM regfile so ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val are real flops, not BSRAM clk-to-out at the head of the EX critical path
motivation:
The champion's worst path (58.3 MHz, 23.29 ns arrival, 14 cells) is
  cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s -> u_id -> u_ex (fwd mux, operand mux)
  -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result_11.
It starts at the register-file RAM, not at an ID/EX flop. Gowin
synthesis logs "Extracting RAM for identifier 'regs'" (reg_file.sv:32),
and the resource count is bsram=6 = 4 for the 2Kx32 dmem + 2 for the
regfile's two read ports. Gowin can only read BSRAM synchronously, so
it folds the ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val registers into the BSRAM read (the
address is sampled at the ID->EX edge). It then rebuilds the
write-first bypass and the ID/EX flush/hold clear as extra logic after
the BSRAM output (the u_id cells on the path). So every EX operand
starts with the BSRAM's slow clock-to-out plus 1-2 LUTs of
bypass/clear, and all of that is in series with the fwd mux, the ALU
and the result mux.
The fetch word comes from a flop (the LFSR in core_bench_si), and ID
only decodes, so ID has plenty of slack. With a regfile that reads
asynchronously, the RAM read and the bypass move into ID, and EX
starts at a real flop (~0.4 ns clk-to-q).

1. reg_file.sv: force the 32x32 array out of block RAM with a Gowin
   attribute on the array, (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *),
   which maps it to RAM16SDP4 LUT-RAM with async read. That is about 32
   SSRAM cells for 2 read ports, well inside the 10k LUT budget. If
   Gowin ignores the attribute or the reset-clear loop blocks
   distributed-RAM mapping, use syn_ramstyle = "registers" instead:
   1024 FFs plus 2x32 32:1 MUX_LUT trees, about 700 LUTs, still in
   budget. Keep the write-first bypass and the x0 = 0 behaviour
   bit-identical. libgwsyn.so (Gowin 1.9.11.03) contains the
   syn_ramstyle attribute and the values BLOCK_RAM, DISTRIBUTED_RAM and
   REGISTERS. Check the synthesis log and resource report:
   bsram should be 4, and SSRAM or FF count should rise.
2. Nothing else changes functionally. ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val become
   ordinary DFFs with sync clear/CE (free in Gowin DFFRE), fed by
   imem_data (flop) -> LUT-RAM read -> depth mux -> bypass mux. That is
   about 4-5 levels, all in ID, which has slack.
Expected result: EX paths start at a flop, not at BSRAM tCO plus the
rebuilt bypass/clear LUTs. That should take roughly 3-5 ns off a
~17 ns period, until the next path limits: MEM/WB -> WB mux -> fwd
mux -> ALU -> alu_result, or the AGU -> dmem BSRAM address setup.

that the worst path no longer starts at u_rf/regs. If the new worst
path is MEM/WB.read_data/alu_result -> wb mux -> fwd mux, also
register a pre-muxed wb_data copy in MEM/WB (read_data vs alu_result
selected in MEM) as a cheap follow-up cut.

title: Move MUL into the MEM stage with a MUL-use interlock, and squash redirect wrong-path in EX instead of clearing ID/EX
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (p0 55.6 MHz) shows two
near-tied EX paths. Both start at the regfile BSRAM (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s,
tC2Q 2.26 ns), which Gowin maps with the ID/EX rs?_val register as the
BSRAM read register, followed by 2 LUTs of Gowin-made bypass/clear logic
(id_ex_w.rs?_val_*_s14/_s13 plus shadow flops *_s1/_s100):
  1) 23.29 ns, 14 cells: BSRAM -> bypass -> fwd mux (2 LUT) -> alu_a ->
     MULH sign-extend LUT -> DSP prod_65_s1 (3.76 ns, 0.92 ns route in)
     -> 7-LUT ALU/div/jump result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result. Paths 1-5,
     7, 11, 12, 14 and 16 all go through the DSP.
  2) 22.71 ns, 11 cells: BSRAM -> bypass -> fwd mux -> branch compare /
     redirect (u_if/n69, 4 LUT) -> u_id/n127 flush -> a fanout-33 clear
     LUT with a 2 ns route -> ID/EX rs?_val shadow flops. Paths 6, 8-10,
     13, 15 and 17-24 are this one: the EX redirect drives the synchronous
     clear of the whole ID/EX register (flush_id, and in.valid=!redirect ->
     reg_q <= '0), including the flops Gowin adds behind the regfile BSRAM.
They are 0.6 ns apart. Per LESSONS (r2s0), cutting only one leaves Fmax
flat, so both are cut here.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two changes to the pipeline structure, each removing one of the tied paths:

(A) MUL* runs in MEM, not EX. The 33x33 signed product takes its operands
from EX/MEM.rs1_val / rs2_val (already post-forward flops; for MUL*
alu_a = rs1 and alu_b = rs2 because is_auipc = alu_src = 0). The sa/sb
sign flags and the lo/hi select come from EX/MEM.ctrl.alu_op. mem_stage
muxes `is_mul ? prod : in.alu_result` into MEM/WB.alu_result, so
wb_w_data / fwd_mem_wb are unchanged. The DSP leaves the EX cone and the
EX result mux loses four op arms. The MEM path is EX/MEM flop -> DSP ->
2:1 mux -> MEM/WB, about 8 ns. The ALTOPS stand-ins move to the same place
and are computed on the same EX/MEM rs?_val, so formal stays consistent.
A MUL result can't be forwarded from EX/MEM, so a consumer right behind a
MUL takes a 1-cycle interlock like load-use. In hazard_unit, use
(id_ex_mem_read | id_ex_is_mul) in the load-use compare, where is_mul is a
decoder bit registered in ID/EX. Forwarding from MEM/WB then covers
distance 2. Clear EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write-based EX forwarding for MUL (or
never select fwd_ex_mem when the EX/MEM op is a MUL; the interlock makes
that case unreachable). Keep the alu.sv MUL arms, or move them into a
small mul unit in mem_stage; test_alu.py vectors must still pass against
whichever module owns the multiply.
Cost: static CoreMark has 28 MUL*, and 13 are immediately followed by
their consumer. MUL is dense only in matrix_*, so the extra bubbles should
cost about 1-3% of cycles. This is far less than r1s1's 2 unconditional
stall cycles per MUL.

(B) Squash wrong-path instructions in EX rather than clearing ID/EX on
redirect. Remove `redirect` from flush_id and from if_stage out.valid so
ID/EX always captures the fetched word on a redirect. Add one flop,
squash_q <= redirect && !stall_ex_mem (set when the branch/jump actually
leaves EX, reset 0). In EX, effective valid = in.valid && !squash_q, and
it gates everything with side effects: redirect, EX/MEM valid,
ctrl.reg_write / mem_read / mem_write, divider start and div_busy, and
the load-use/MUL-use compare in hazard_unit (so a squashed load or MUL
doesn't cause a bubble). Also stop resetting/clearing the ID/EX data
fields (pc, rs?_val, imm, instr, rd, rs?_addr, hit bits). Only valid and
the ctrl side-effect bits get the reset / bubble clear. The regfile BSRAM
then needs only the write-first bypass behind it, not the clear/shadow
flops. The redirect cone ends at the PC / imem BSRAM address and one
flop, not a fanout-200 synchronous clear. Load-use / imem-stall bubbles
still clear valid+ctrl as today. Cycle count is unchanged: the squashed
slot was already a bubble.

Run `make timing TARGET=bench` after both cuts. The next wall is expected
to be BSRAM -> fwd mux -> adder -> result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result, about
15-16 ns of data path against 17.96 ns now. If a third path ties, trim it
in the same iteration. The cheapest option is a one-hot ALU result select
registered in ID/EX (AND-OR of sum/logic/shift/slt/pc+4/div), which
flattens the 7-LUT result mux.
Expected: Fmax 58.3 -> ~66-68 MHz median (+13-17%), minus 1-3% cycles
from the MUL-use interlock.

changes.description: Own the 33x33 MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU multiply (and its ALTOPS stand-ins) on EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val; mux the product into MEM/WB.alu_result when EX/MEM holds a MUL*.
Drop the MUL* arms (and prod) from the EX ALU so the DSP and its operand sign-extend leave the EX result cone; or split them into a mul unit that mem_stage instantiates.

title: Zero-bubble IF predecode + 64-entry BTFN-seeded bimodal BHT on the r2s0 base, with the mispredict XOR folded into the comparator and redirect cut off the ID/EX data-flop resets
motivation:
The champion (hyp-20260929-001-r2s0, 4,491,817 cycles, 129.87) still
resolves every control transfer in EX. There is no IF/ID flop: the word
fetched at PC is decoded in the same cycle and captured into ID/EX. So
every taken branch, JAL or JALR costs exactly one bubble, because the
pc+4 word fetched while the transfer sits in EX is squashed. The ISS
trace of the timed CoreMark window (see r1s2) shows 2.92M instructions,
294k taken conditional branches, 49k JAL and 13.7k JALR (all `ret`). That
is ~357k redirect bubbles, about 8% of all cycles.

Earlier predictor runs:
  * r1s2 put an IF predecode with a 64-entry BTFN-seeded bimodal BHT and a
    1-bubble combinational mispredict redirect on the slow (~5.4 MHz)
    base. Cycles fell from 4,491,485 to 4,194,484 (-6.6%), exactly as the
    trace model predicted. That run said nothing about timing.
  * r2s2 used a registered redirect with a 2-bubble mispredict, on a base
    without registered forwarding hits. It reached only 53.7 MHz and lost
    to r2s0.
LESSONS says to port the predictor onto r2s0 and check whether the
redirect -> PC path is critical there. I ran `make timing` on the
champion (place option 0, 55.6 MHz):
  * Paths 1-5 (22.8-23.3 ns) run regfile BSRAM DO -> bypass -> forward
    mux -> alu_a -> DSP multiplier -> result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
  * Path 6 (22.71 ns, only 0.58 ns behind) is the branch-redirect path:
    regfile DO -> forward mux rs1 -> 4 LUT levels of branch compare that
    end in u_if (the `out.valid = !(flush || redirect)` cone) ->
    u_id/n127 (the ID/EX clear condition) -> a fanout-33 net (2.0 ns of
    routing) into the SYNC-RESET pins of the ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val data
    flops.
So the redirect cone is effectively tied with the multiplier. A
predictor that adds even one LUT level to it (mispredict = cond ^
pred_taken) or widens the PC mux behind it would give back ~3-5% Fmax
and eat most of the ~7% IPC gain. The IF side, by contrast, has plenty
of slack. In the timed harness io_imemData is an LFSR flop
(fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so flop -> opcode/imm select -> one 32-bit
adder -> PC mux is roughly half a clock period.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Port r1s2's zero-bubble next-PC prediction onto r2s0. Keep all of r2s0's
timing cuts. Build the mispredict path so the EX redirect cone gets
SHORTER than today instead of longer.

1. IF prediction (if_stage.sv). Predecode io_imemData in the fetch cycle:
   is_jal = opcode 1101111; is_br = opcode 1100011 with funct3 not 2/3.
   The immediate is J when instr[3] is set, otherwise B. One 32-bit adder
   computes pred_sum = pc + imm.
   BHT: 64 x 2-bit counters in flops, indexed by pc[7:2] and read from the
   PC register in parallel with the fetch. They store "disagree with
   BTFN": predict = instr[31] ^ ctr[1]. Reset is '0 ("strongly agree"), so
   a cold branch predicts backward-taken, forward-not-taken.
   pred_taken = !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_br && predict)). A misaligned
   target is never predicted, so EX's misalign trap (no redirect, pc_next
   = pc+4) is unchanged.
   PC priority: reset > redirect ? redirect_target : stall ? hold :
   pred_taken ? pred_sum : pc+4. `redirect` stays the LAST mux select, so
   the new inputs sit in front of it and the EX -> PC depth does not
   change.
   IF also emits pred_taken and alt_pc = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_sum,
   the other direction of the fetched transfer.
   ID/EX captures a valid word only when !dmem_stall, !load_use,
   !div_busy, !imem_stall and !redirect, which is exactly stall_if = 0 &&
   !redirect. So the pred_taken stored in ID/EX always matches what the
   PC register actually did. No extra qualification is needed.

2. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv id_ex_t). Capture alt_pc and three
   precomputed control bits:
     br_inv_q    = funct3[0] ^ pred_taken   (BNE/BGE/BGEU are the
                                             inverted BEQ/BLT/BLTU)
     br_redir_q  = is_branch && !imm[1]     (misaligned-if-taken
                                             branches can never redirect)
     jalr_q      = is_jalr
   Also cut `redirect` off the ID/EX data flops. Only valid and ctrl (plus
   the new control bits) are cleared on flush or !valid. pc, rs1_val,
   rs2_val, imm, instr, alt_pc, rs?_addr and rd are loaded under !stall
   alone, with no clear. A bubble's data fields are dead: ctrl.reg_write =
   mem_read = mem_write = is_branch = is_jump = 0 and valid = 0. The
   forwarding hits are qualified by the live reg_write and load-use by
   ctrl.mem_read, so stale data or rd in a bubble cannot hit. This removes
   the fanout-33 sync-reset net at the end of timing path 6.

3. EX (ex_stage.sv). Only a mispredict redirects:
     base_cmp = funct3[2:1]==0 ? eq : funct3[1] ? ltu : lt
     redirect = (br_redir_q && (base_cmp ^ br_inv_q))
              || (jalr_q && !jalr_sum[1])
   This has the same LUT depth as today's compare and invert. The
   branch_taken -> misalign_branch -> redirect chain and the pc+imm adder
   bits are gone from the redirect cone. An aligned JAL never redirects,
   because IF always takes it; a misaligned JAL still traps with no
   redirect.
   redirect_target = jalr_q ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : alt_pc_q. This
   replaces today's 3-way is_jump/is_jalr/branch_target mux.
   The EX pc+imm adders, branch_taken and pc_next stay only for RVFI
   pc_next and the misalign trap bits; RVFI-only logic is pruned.
   Every RVFI field is unchanged. JALR keeps its 1-bubble redirect. There
   is no RAS: 13.7k `ret`s is 0.3% of cycles and not worth another 32-bit
   compare on this near-critical cone.

4. BHT update. Register (valid, pc[7:2], actual_taken ^ instr[31]) one
   cycle after EX, then apply the saturating inc/dec. Gate the write with
   EX valid && is_branch && !stall_ex_mem, so a branch held in EX by a
   dmem stall updates only once. The comparator then never fans out into
   the 128 counter flops. The trace shows no measurable cost from the
   one-cycle delay.

5. Hazard unit: unchanged. flush_if = redirect || imem_stall still kills
   the single wrong-path fetch, and redirect still overrides stall at the
   PC.

Expected: cycles go from ~4.49M to ~4.19M (-6.6%, the r1s2 measurement on
this identical cycle model). Fmax stays at or slightly above the
champion's because path 6 loses its misalign chain and its reset fanout,
while the multiplier paths are untouched. Net: about +7% fitness.
The implementer must run `make timing` and confirm two things: no
u_if/pc or ID/EX-clear path has overtaken the u_alu/prod paths, and the
lfsr -> pred_sum -> PC path is well below 23 ns.

title: Flop-to-ALU operands: registered WB data, pre-qualified one-hot forward selects and ID pre-selected ALU operands
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (r3s0, place option 0, 72.3 MHz)
shows three near-tied path families. All three start in the same
EX operand-select logic:
  1. 19.126 ns  u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.mem_to_reg (fanout 40, 1.26 ns net)
     -> u_wb w_data mux -> u_ex rs1 fwd (2 LUT levels) -> alu_a
     (auipc) mux -> DSP A input (fanout 72, 1.25 ns net) -> DSP
     (3.76 ns) -> 3-LUT result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
     In this path, 3.8 ns of the 13.8 ns data path is wb mux + fwd +
     operand mux before the ALU even starts.
  2. 19.072 ns  u_ex/reg_q.ctrl.reg_write (fanout 48) -> forward_unit
     qualification LUT (fanout 32) -> rs1 fwd -> alu_a -> ALU
     shifter/adder -> 5-LUT result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
  3. 18.93 ns   the same reg_write -> select LUTs -> rs1 fwd -> branch
     comparator carry chain -> redirect -> u_if valid -> ID/EX sync clear
     (~260 flops: pc_31, valid, ctrl.*).
Most of the time before the ALU/comparator/DSP goes to three things.
The WB write-data mux is combinational after MEM/WB. The forward
selects are ANDed with the live EX/MEM and MEM/WB reg_write bits in
EX. The auipc/alu_src operand mux sits after the forward mux. These
are 3-4 LUT levels plus two high-fanout nets on every EX path, and
all of them can be moved into MEM and ID, which have slack. The
change does not alter cycle count (4.49M cycles).

Most of the time before the ALU/comparator/DSP goes to three things.
The WB write-data mux is combinational after MEM/WB. The forward

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Timing-only change. The goal is that every EX operand (ALU A/B, DSP
inputs, branch compare, AGU, JALR, store data) is ONE LUT5-level
3:1 mux whose data and select inputs are all flops.

1. Registered WB data (mem_stage / core_pkg / wb_stage). Add
   mem_wb_t.wb_data = mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result, selected
   in MEM before the MEM/WB flop. The load path is the dmem BSRAM
   read, then the align/extend LUTs, then this mux, ending at a flop,
   which leaves a lot of slack. wb_stage drives w_data = in.wb_data,
   so fwd_mem_wb, the regfile write data and its write-first bypass
   all come from a flop. hold_wb keeps wb_data, like every other data
   field. read_data/alu_result can be dropped from mem_wb_t.

2. Pre-qualified, priority-resolved forward selects registered in ID
   (id_stage / forward_unit / ex_stage / core_pkg). Today EX computes
   fwd = hit && live_reg_write. Instead, compute the qualification at
   the ID capture edge. That edge is the same edge on which EX/MEM
   captures the producer now in ID/EX, and MEM/WB captures the one
   now in EX/MEM. ID captures only when !stall_id, and stall_id
   covers dmem_stall and div_busy, so EX/MEM and MEM/WB always
   advance on that edge:
     ex_wen_next = id_ex.ctrl.reg_write && !misalign_jump
                   (export from ex_stage. Write it explicitly with
                   misalign_jump only, NOT ctrl_with_trap.reg_write:
                   branches never have reg_write, and going through
                   misalign_branch would pull the branch comparator
                   into the ID cone. div_busy is always 0 on a
                   capture edge.)
     wb_wen_next = ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write && !mem_misalign
                   (export ctrl_with_trap.reg_write from mem_stage;
                   it is built only from EX/MEM flops.)
     hit_ex  = id_ex.rd  != 0 && id_ex.rd  == rs? && ex_wen_next
     hit_mem = ex_mem.rd != 0 && ex_mem.rd == rs? && wb_wen_next
     sel_ex  = hit_ex;  sel_mem = hit_mem && !hit_ex
   Register sel_ex/sel_mem for rs1 and rs2 in ID/EX. They are cleared
   with the bubble. EX muxes become
     rs1 = sel_ex ? ex_mem.alu_result : sel_mem ? mem_wb.wb_data : rs1_val.
   This stays exact across holds, which is the invariant the
   implementer must preserve:
   - During a dmem stall, EX/MEM and MEM/WB keep their data and ctrl
     (MEM/WB only drops valid).
   - A DIV* latches its operands at start.
   - Load-use still bubbles the consumer, and a LOAD in ID/EX never
     gets captured as a sel_ex producer.
   - EX-misalign and MEM-misalign traps are folded in through
     ex_wen_next and wb_wen_next.
   forward_unit reduces to passing through the registered selects, or
   is deleted.

3. ALU operands pre-selected in ID. Add id_ex_t.op_a =
   is_auipc ? pc : rs1_data and op_b = alu_src ? imm : rs2_data, plus
   operand selects
     a_sel_ex/mem = rs1 sel && !is_auipc
     b_sel_ex/mem = rs2 sel && !alu_src.
   EX then feeds the ALU and DSP with
     alu_a = a_sel_ex ? ex_mem.alu_result : a_sel_mem ? wb_data : op_a
   (same shape for B). This removes the alu_a/alu_b mux level and
   splits the fanout-72 DSP/ALU operand net from the branch/AGU/store
   rs1/rs2 nets. Keep rs1_val/rs2_val and the rs1/rs2 forward muxes
   for the branch compare, AGU, JALR, store data, divider and RVFI.
   ALU_LUI still returns b, so LUI is unaffected.

4. Smaller ID/EX flush fanout (path 3 tail). On flush or !in.valid,
   sync-clear only valid, ctrl, rd and the forward/operand select
   bits. Data fields (pc, rs?_val, op_a/op_b, imm, rs?_addr, instr)
   get CE = !stall only. A bubble's stale data reaches no side
   effect:
   - dmem_wen/ren come from ctrl.
   - Cosim flags OOB on dmem only when REn/WEn is set.
   - redirect needs is_branch or is_jump.
   - is_div needs valid.
   - RVFI is gated by valid.
   This cuts the redirect -> clear net from ~260 flops to ~40.

Expected result: the operand head drops from wb mux + 2 fwd LUTs +
operand mux (about 3.5-4 ns including the two high-fanout nets) to
one LUT5 off flops (about 1.2 ns). All three path families lose
2.5-3 ns of ~13.8 ns, which gives an estimated 88-95 MHz vs 76.3
MHz at identical cycles.

The next limiters should be the 5-level ALU result mux (base_out
case + mul/div/jump select) and the DSP. If `make timing` shows the
result mux on top and time remains, register a one-hot result-group
select in ID (add/sub, logic, shift, slt, lui, link, mul) and a
precomputed pc+4 (link) flop in ID/EX. Use an AND-OR in front of
EX/MEM.alu_result, keeping mul_out as the last select. This is
optional; the core of the hypothesis is items 1-4.

LUT/FF cost: about +80 FFs (op_a/op_b, selects, wb_data) and roughly
neutral LUTs, far inside budget.

title: Move the bypass network from EX into ID: ID/EX captures fully resolved ALU operands (2-ahead result forwarded in ID, imm/pc pre-selected); EX keeps one 2:1 bypass from EX/MEM on a registered select
motivation:
The champion (r3s0, 76.3 MHz, 169.86) has this worst path (19.126 ns
arrival, 9 cells):
  cpu/u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.mem_to_reg -> u_wb (w_data mux) -> u_ex (3:1
  fwd mux) -> alu_a/alu_b mux (auipc / alu_src) -> u_alu -> EX
  result mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
Every EX path starts with the same front end, about 3-4 LUT levels in
series before the adder: MEM/WB mem_to_reg -> WB mux (the net fans
out to 32 w_data bits, the regfile write port, the regfile bypass and
both EX forward muxes), then the 3:1 forward mux on fwd_rs?_sel, then
the operand mux. The same front end also feeds the branch comparator
-> redirect -> PC / ID-EX flush cone, the rs1+imm AGU -> dmem BSRAM
address, and the DSP multiplier inputs. So the near-tied paths
behind this one share the head too. LESSONS r3s1 says to fix the
shared head before reworking the tails.
The ID stage now has slack. Since r3s0 the regfile is async LUT-RAM
and the fetch word comes from a flop, so ID only does decode, the
LUT-RAM read and the write-first bypass. ID can absorb the forward
and operand selection that EX does now.
How this differs from r2s1, which also had a 2:1 EX bypass and scored
+2.5%: r2s1 removed MEM/WB, so dmem BSRAM -> load-align -> regfile
write-first bypass ran in one cycle. It had no AGU, so the ALU result
was also the BSRAM address. It also sat on the BSRAM regfile. None of
that applies here. This change keeps 5 stages, the AGU and the
LUT-RAM regfile, and only moves where the 2-ahead forward and the
operand select happen.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the bypass network across the ID/EX boundary, the way
FPGA-tuned cores do register-read-stage bypassing. Cycle count stays
the same (~4.49M): every forwarding case stays covered, and load-use
is still the only interlock.

Timing of producers relative to a consumer C:
  - 3-ahead producer: in MEM/WB while C is in ID. The regfile's
    existing write-first bypass already covers it.
  - 2-ahead producer: in EX/MEM (the MEM stage) while C is in ID. Its
    final value is known during that cycle: EX/MEM.alu_result, or for
    a load the load-aligned dmem_rdata. Forward it in ID, not in EX.
  - 1-ahead producer: in ID/EX while C is in ID, and in EX/MEM while C
    is in EX. This is the only bypass left in EX: a 2:1 mux from the
    registered EX/MEM.alu_result. A load here is already bubbled by
    load-use, so after the bubble the load sits in MEM and is covered
    by the ID-stage 2-ahead forward.

Changes:
1. MEM stage computes one `mem_result = mem_to_reg ? load_data :
   alu_result` (load-align + sext + select, one mux tree). It feeds
   (a) the ID-stage forward, and (b) a new pre-muxed MEM/WB.wb_data
   flop. WB's w_data then comes straight from a flop, and the
   mem_to_reg -> 32-bit WB mux is gone from the regfile bypass path.
   Qualify the forward with the live `ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write &&
   !mem_misalign` so a misaligned load/store trap stays exact (the
   same rule as today's late qualification).
2. ID: fwd_mem_rs? = (ex_mem.rd != 0) && (ex_mem.rd == rs?_addr) &&
   mem_wen_live. Then:
     rs1_val_d = fwd_mem_rs1 ? mem_result : rf_rs1   (store data, branch cmp, RVFI)
     rs2_val_d = fwd_mem_rs2 ? mem_result : rf_rs2
     op_a_d    = is_auipc/jump ? pc : is_lui ? 0 : rs1_val_d
     op_b_d    = alu_src ? imm : rs2_val_d
   Put the late-arriving mem_result select last in each mux (for
   example op_b_d = (fwd_mem_rs2 && !alu_src) ? mem_result :
   (alu_src ? imm : rf_rs2)), so the BSRAM -> align -> forward path is
   about 4 LUTs into an ID/EX flop.
   Registered EX selects: op_a_hit = rs1_hit_ex && !(auipc|lui|jump),
   op_b_hit = rs2_hit_ex && !alu_src. The existing rs?_hit_ex compare
   against ID/EX.rd stays as it is. rs?_hit_mem is no longer needed.
3. EX: rs1 = (rs1_hit_ex && ex_mem.reg_write) ? ex_mem.alu_result :
   in.rs1_val, and the same for rs2, alu_a (op_a_hit) and alu_b
   (op_b_hit). Each is a single LUT4: 2 data bits, the hit flop and
   the reg_write flop. The 3:1 fwd mux and the separate operand mux
   both leave the ALU / AGU / comparator / DSP front end. The
   fwd_mem_wb input and the MEM/WB forward source are deleted.
   forward_unit.sv shrinks to the two AND gates, or is folded into
   ex_stage. Keep the file so test_pipeline's source list still
   builds, or update the list.
4. Optional, same idea (do it if it is clean): JAL/JALR link value.
   With op_a = pc and op_b = 4 pre-selected in ID and alu_op = ADD,
   the ALU produces pc+4 itself, and the `is_jump ? pc+4` arm leaves
   the EX/MEM.alu_result select. The jump target still comes from its
   own pc+imm / rs1+imm adders; they read in.imm and the forwarded
   rs1, not op_b. LUI likewise becomes op_a = 0 + imm via ADD. Keep
   ALU_LUI in alu.sv because test_alu.py covers it.
5. Optional, cuts redirect fanout: on flush/bubble, sync-clear only the
   ID/EX control part (valid, ctrl, rd, hit bits), not the 32-bit data
   fields (pc, rs?_val, op_a/op_b, imm, instr). A bubble has
   valid = 0, reg_write = mem_* = is_branch = is_jump = 0, so garbage
   data is inert. This keeps the extra 64 op_a/op_b flops off the
   redirect -> flush fanout, which r3s1 found costly at ~200 loads.

Invariants to keep:
  - dmem stall: ID/EX and EX/MEM hold together, and ID does not
    capture while stall_id is high. A consumer in ID therefore
    forwards the stalled load's data only on the cycle the bus
    delivers. MEM/WB's hold keeps valid = 0, which blocks a second
    regfile write. The EX-side MEM/WB "retain data for forwarding"
    requirement disappears, because operands are captured at ID time.
    Keep the hold anyway; it is harmless.
  - div_busy: the DIV sits in ID/EX, EX/MEM gets bubbles
    (reg_write = 0), and the consumer in ID reads the regfile, which
    the older producers have drained into. When the DIV result lands
    in EX/MEM, the consumer's registered rs?_hit_ex selects it. The
    divider latches operands in its first EX cycle, as today.
  - RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata = EX-stage post-bypass rs1/rs2, or the
    divider's latched copies. Semantics do not change.

Expected timing effect: the EX critical path goes from flop -> WB mux
-> fwd 3:1 -> operand mux -> ALU -> result mux (9 cells) to flop ->
2:1 bypass -> ALU -> result mux. That removes 2-3 cells and one
high-fanout net from the worst path and from its tied siblings (branch
redirect, AGU -> BSRAM, DSP). The new ID paths are LUT-RAM read ->
bypass -> op mux, and BSRAM rdata -> align -> mem_result -> forward
mux. Both are about 4 levels, shorter than the ALU + result mux path.
Estimated Fmax is 76 -> ~88-92 MHz with an unchanged cycle count.
Area is about +100 FF and +150 LUT, far inside the 10k budget.
Implementer: run `make timing TARGET=bench` after the change. If the
top path moves to the BSRAM -> load-align -> ID forward chain, first
check that the mem_result select is the last mux before the ID/EX
flop. If the top path is the EX result mux, do step 4.

title: Zero-bubble IF predictor on the r3s0 base, with a timing-neutral EX side: alt_pc carried from IF, mispredict inversion precomputed in ID, redirect off the ID/EX data-flop clears
motivation:
The champion (r3s0, 76.3 MHz median, 4,491,817 cycles, 169.86) still
resolves every control transfer in EX. There is no IF/ID flop: the
word fetched at PC is decoded in the same cycle and captured into
ID/EX. So every taken branch, JAL and JALR costs one bubble, because
the pc+4 word fetched while the transfer sits in EX is squashed. The
ISS trace (r1s2) counts about 294k taken branches, 49k JAL and 13.7k
JALR in the timed window, about 357k bubbles or 8% of all cycles.
Measured history: r1s2 (IF predecode + 64-entry BTFN-seeded bimodal
BHT) cut cycles 4,491,485 -> 4,194,484 (-6.6%), in line with the trace
model. r3s2 ported that design onto r2s0. Its worst path was still
the same regfile-BSRAM -> ALU -> alu_result path as its base, at
55.1 MHz, which is inside r2s0's own seed spread (55.6-58.3). So the
predictor added no new critical path; it lost only because its base
was 25% slower than r3s0's. LESSONS says to port it onto r3s0 once
timing-only cuts stop paying, and to accept it only if no new u_if/pc
or ID/EX path shows up near the top. In the timed harness
io_imemData is an LFSR flop (fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so the IF
predecode + adder + PC mux path starts at a flop and has roughly half
a 13 ns period of slack.

Measured on the champion RTL (`make timing`, place option 0, 72.3 MHz):
  * paths 1-7 (19.13-18.94 ns): MEM/WB.mem_to_reg or EX/MEM.reg_write
    -> fwd mux -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
  * paths 8+ (18.93 ns, only 0.2 ns behind, dozens of endpoints): the
    REDIRECT cone. EX/MEM.reg_write -> fwd mux rs1 -> 32-bit
    carry-chain compare -> FIVE LUT levels in u_if/n329_* (the redirect
    = (taken||jump) && !misalign_fault cone plus out.valid) ->
    u_id/n127 (ID/EX clear, fanout 157, 1.24 ns route) -> the RESET
    pins of every ID/EX flop (pc_31, valid, ctrl.*).
So the redirect cone is effectively tied with the ALU path. The
predictor's EX side replaces it with a shorter one. A mispredict
test is base_cmp ^ inv with the inversion and the misalign
qualification precomputed in ID, which is about 2 LUTs instead of 5.
The fanout-157 data-flop clear is also removed. This design makes
the redirect cone shorter instead of loading it further. The ALU path
is untouched, so Fmax should hold at the champion's ~76 MHz while
cycles fall by ~6.6%.

    = (taken||jump) && !misalign_fault cone plus out.valid) ->
    u_id/n127 (ID/EX clear, fanout 157, 1.24 ns route) -> the RESET
    pins of every ID/EX flop (pc_31, valid, ctrl.*).
So the redirect cone is effectively tied with the ALU path. The
predictor's EX side replaces it with a shorter one. A mispredict
test is base_cmp ^ inv with the inversion and the misalign
qualification precomputed in ID, which is about 2 LUTs instead of 5.
The fanout-157 data-flop clear is also removed. This design makes
the redirect cone shorter instead of loading it further. The ALU path
is untouched, so Fmax should hold at the champion's ~76 MHz while
cycles fall by ~6.6%.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply r1s2/r3s2's zero-bubble next-PC prediction to the r3s0 base.
Build the EX side so the redirect cone is no longer than it is today
(fewer levels if possible). Expected cycles about 4.19M (-6.6%); the
gain is kept only if Fmax stays at or above ~74.5 MHz.

1. IF (if_stage.sv). Predecode io_imemData in the fetch cycle:
   is_jal = opcode 1101111; is_br = opcode 1100011 with funct3 not 2/3.
   imm = J-imm if instr[3] is set, otherwise B-imm. One 32-bit adder
   computes pred_tgt = pc + imm. An optional second adder variant is
   pc+immB and pc+immJ in parallel with a select after them; use it
   only if make timing shows the IF adder near the top.
   BHT: 64 x 2-bit "disagree with BTFN" counters in flops, indexed by
   pc[7:2] and read from the PC register, reset '0.
   dir = instr[31] ^ ctr[1].
   pred_taken = !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_br && dir)). A misaligned
   target is never predicted, so it traps in EX exactly as today.
   PC next-state, with redirect as the LAST select because it arrives
   latest:
     pc_nr = stall ? pc : (pred_taken ? pred_tgt : pc+4)
     pc_d  = redirect ? redirect_target : pc_nr
   Emit pred_taken and alt_pc = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_tgt (the
   direction not taken). This is correct across stalls: the PC and
   ID/EX advance together and use the same pred_taken, and a held PC
   re-predicts its own word.
2. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv). Register pred_taken and alt_pc[31:0]
   into ID/EX. Also precompute into ID/EX:
     br_inv   = funct3[0] ^ pred_taken
     br_redir = is_branch && !imm[1]
     jalr     = is_jalr
   Split the ID/EX register. valid, ctrl and the new control bits keep
   the reset/flush/!valid sync clear. The data fields (pc, rs?_val,
   imm, instr, alt_pc, rd, rs?_addr, hit bits) load on !stall only
   and have no sync clear, so redirect only reaches ~20 control flops
   instead of ~200. Hit bits are safe because ex_mem_w_en/mem_wb_w_en
   qualify them, and a bubble has reg_write = 0.
3. EX (ex_stage.sv). Base compare: EQ, LT or LTU, chosen by one-hot
   selects decoded from funct3[2:1] in ID and registered (sel_eq,
   sel_lt, sel_ltu). This keeps a decode LUT out of the post-compare
   cone. Then:
     mispredict_br = br_redir_q && (base_cmp ^ br_inv_q)
     redirect      = mispredict_br || (jalr_q && !jalr_sum[1])
     redirect_target = jalr_q ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : alt_pc_q
   alt_pc_q is a flop, so the EX pc+imm adder leaves the redirect
   target path. An aligned JAL never redirects (it is always
   predicted). A misaligned branch or JAL is never predicted and still
   traps. branch_taken, pc_next, the misalign traps and all RVFI fields
   are computed from the real outcome exactly as today. BHT update
   request {valid, pc[7:2], taken ^ instr[31]} is gated by
   in.valid && is_branch && !stall && !div_busy. It is REGISTERED (one
   flop stage) before it touches the counters, so branch_cond does not
   fan into the BHT CE/D cone.
4. Hazard/forward unchanged. flush_if = redirect || imem_stall and
   out.valid = !(flush || redirect) keep their meaning, because a
   "redirect" is now only a mispredict or a JALR.

Timing guardrails for the implementer (run `make timing` on the
diff): the r3s0 worst path is MEM/WB.mem_to_reg -> wb mux -> fwd mux
-> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result (9 cells). The new logic must not put a
u_if/pc or BHT path within ~0.5 ns of it. If the redirect -> PC path
becomes top-3, first make sure redirect is the final mux select on
pc_d (and on the IF valid bit), not buried under stall/pred. If the
IF predecode -> adder -> PC path is top-3, use the two-adder variant.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-003-r4s2 (regression, +6.37%): The zero-bubble IF predictor ported onto r3s0 returned +6.37%, almost exactly r1s2's IPC-only +6.44%, so if cycles fell to ~4.19M its Fmax held at ~75.8 MHz (champion 76.3) and the timing-neutral EX side worked; that EX side carried alt_pc from IF (no EX pc+imm adder on the redirect target), computed mispredict = br_redir && (base_cmp ^ br_inv) with the one-hot EQ/LT/LTU selects and the inversion registered in ID, let only a misaligned jump (not a branch) clear reg_write so the compare stays out of EX/MEM.reg_write, registered the BHT update, and had the redirect sync-clear only the ID/EX control flops; it scored as a regression only because same-round sibling r4s1 gained +23.5% from timing, the fourth predictor port (r1s2, r2s2, r3s2, r4s2) to lose a race against a pure-timing sibling, and because fitness = 10·MHz/Mcycles multiplies orthogonal gains (~1.235 × 1.064 ≈ +31% over r3s0), stack this diff on the r4s1 base (which already has the control-only ID/EX clear) instead of racing it again, then re-run `make timing`, because at ~94 MHz (10.6 ns) the io_imemData -> predecode -> pc+imm -> PC path, whose slack was only estimated against a 13 ns period, may reach the top, and if it does, switch to the two-adder variant (pc+immB and pc+immJ in parallel, select after).

title: Trim all three tied EX tails: one-hot ALU result AND-OR, 1-LUT DSP tail, ID-registered branch selects + squash flop (redirect off the ID/EX clear)
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (r4s1, 93.1-94.2 MHz)
shows 25+ setup paths all within 0.1 ns of each other (10.61-10.71 ns
data delay against the 5 ns constraint). They fall into three
families, so, per the r2s0 lesson, cutting only one of them leaves
Fmax flat:
 (1) BRANCH -> REDIRECT -> ID/EX CLEAR (paths 1,2,5,9,10,16-25):
     EX/MEM.alu_result_1 -> rs1 bypass LUT -> one 32-cell carry-chain
     compare (~1.6 ns incl. entry) -> 1.77 ns route -> 3 LUTs
     (n329_s5/s3/s0 in u_if: the branch_op case select, is_branch &&
     cond, misalign, redirect, and out.valid = !(flush||redirect),
     fanout 35) -> u_id clear LUT (fanout 23) -> RESET pin of every
     ID/EX control flop. About 5.8 ns of the path is after the chain.
 (2) ALU RESULT MUX (path 3): ID/EX.op_b_hit (fanout 33) -> alu_b
     bypass -> 2.67 ns route -> one ALU cell -> FIVE LUT levels
     (n705_s18/s10/s4/s1/s0) -> EX/MEM.alu_result_25. The 5-level tail
     is the 11-way case(alu_op) base_out mux on a 5-bit binary op
     plus the div_done / mul_sel selects.
 (3) DSP (paths 4,6-8,11-15): EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write (fanout 133) ->
     alu_a bypass LUT -> 2.86 ns route -> DSP 3.76 ns -> LUT
     (prod lo/hi select, op==MUL compare) -> 0.76 ns route -> LUT
     (mul_sel ? mul_out : div/base) -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
None of these tails needs to be as deep as it is. Every select they
use can be decoded in ID and registered, where it is off the path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Timing-only change. Cycle count stays at ~4.49M: same forwarding,
same load-use rule, same 2-bubble redirect.

A. ALU result as a one-hot AND-OR (family 2). In ID, decode
   dec_alu_op into registered ID/EX bits (new id_ex_t fields, not
   cleared on bubble since a bubble's result is never used):
     r_sum, r_sub       ADD / SUB (one adder: a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub)
     r_log, r_lop[1:0]  AND / OR / XOR / PASS_B (LUI) -> one LUT4/bit
     r_sh, r_shop[1:0]  SLL / SRL / SRA
     r_slt, r_uns       SLT / SLTU from one 33-bit subtract, bit 32
     r_mlo, r_mhi       MUL vs MULH/MULHSU/MULHU; plus registered
                        sa / sb DSP sign-extension flags
   base = ({32{r_sum}} & sum) | ({32{r_log}} & logic)
        | ({32{r_sh}} & shift) | {31'b0, r_slt & lt}
        | ({32{div_done}} & div_result)
   That is 2 LUT levels after the adder/shifter instead of 5.
B. DSP tail in one LUT5 (family 3):
     alu_result_d = r_mhi ? prod[63:32] : (r_mlo ? prod[31:0] : base)
   With registered selects this is LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5 after the DSP
   instead of 2 LUT4s with a 0.76 ns route between them. Optional: give
   the DSP its own copy of the alu_a / alu_b bypass muxes
   (syn_keep), and give the bypass muxes duplicated EX/MEM.reg_write
   flops (syn_preserve, e.g. one per operand) to break the fanout-133
   net. Keep them only if `make timing` shows they help.
C. Branch resolve (family 1). Decode in ID and register:
     br_eq = BEQ|BNE, br_inv = BNE|BGE|BGEU, br_uns = BLTU|BGEU,
     br_go = is_branch && !imm[1], jal_go = JAL && !imm[1],
     jal_bad = JAL && imm[1].
   (pc[1:0] is always 00: misaligned targets trap without redirecting
   and there is no C extension. B/J imm[0] = 0, so target[1] = imm[1].)
   In EX: lt = bit 32 of {~br_uns&rs1[31], rs1} - {~br_uns&rs2[31], rs2}
   (one chain; the extension bit enters at the MSB end), and eq in
   parallel.
     redirect = br_eq ? ((br_go' & (eq ^ br_inv)) | jmp')
                      : ((br_go' & (lt ^ br_inv)) | jmp')
   is two LUT4s plus a MUX2_LUT5, where br_go' / jmp' already contain
   the squash / valid qualification (flops only) and jalr_ok =
   is_jalr && !(rs1[1] ^ imm[1] ^ (rs1[0] & imm[0])). The misalign
   trap terms (is_illegal, reg_write clear, pc_next = pc+4) use the
   same imm[1] / jalr bits. branch_target / jump_target values and
   EX/MEM.pc_next are unchanged.
D. Squash flop: take redirect off the ID/EX clear (family 1 tail).
   ID/EX captures the wrong-path word in the redirect cycle like any
   other word. squash_q <= redirect (holds while stall_id; reset 0)
   marks it dead for its one cycle in EX:
     - EX: live = in.valid && !squash_q gates EX/MEM.valid,
       EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write / mem_read / mem_write, redirect (folded
       into br_go' / jmp'), and the divider's is_div / start.
     - hazard_unit's id_ex_mem_read = ctrl.mem_read && !squash_q (no
       spurious load-use stall behind a squashed load).
     - if_stage out.valid = !imem_stall; flush_if = imem_stall;
       flush_id = load_use && !dmem_stall. The PC keeps "redirect
       overrides stall".
   Redirect then drives only the 32 PC-mux LUTs and squash_q. It
   stops driving the u_if valid LUT, the u_id clear LUT and ~30
   control-flop RESET pins. An ID-side rs?_hit_ex against a squashed
   rd is harmless because EX qualifies it with EX/MEM.reg_write,
   which is 0 for the squashed op. The ID 2-ahead forward uses
   mem_fwd_en (the same 0). Under a dmem stall ID/EX and squash_q hold
   together, and a held branch re-fires redirect each cycle (pc <=
   target is idempotent), the same as today.

Expected result: family 1 loses ~2-3 LUT levels after the chain
(~2 ns), family 2 loses ~3 LUT levels (~2.5 ns), and family 3 loses
~1 LUT + route (~1 ns). That puts the DSP path at ~9.7 ns, so ~100-104
MHz, a +6..+10% fitness gain at unchanged cycles. The result is
bounded by the DSP family and by second-tier paths (ID mem_result
forward, JALR target -> PC) that the top-25 report does not show.
Re-run `make timing` after A-D, then apply the optional B duplicates
only if the DSP family is still on top.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-001-r5s0 (regression, +9.25%): Trimming all three tied EX tails on r4s1 landed on its estimate (~103 MHz if cycles stayed at ~4.49M) but lost to same-round sibling r5s1 (+14.4%); r5s0 used a one-hot AND-OR ALU result on ID-registered selects, a 1-LUT DSP tail on registered mlo/mhi, ID-registered branch selects, and a squash_q flop so the redirect no longer drives the ID/EX clear; r5s1 made the same ALU-result and squash cuts but also moved the MUL/DIV result select into MEM behind a 1-cycle MUL-use interlock (r3s1 measured that at ~+0.8% cycles); r5s0's own analysis predicted that once the other tails were cut, the in-EX DSP path (bypass head, then the fixed ~3.8 ns DSP) would set the limit, and no tail trimming removes that floor, so r1s1's finding that MUL is not the EX bottleneck held only at ~47 MHz (and r1s1 paid 2 stalls per MUL); near 100 MHz, give the MUL its own pipeline stage with a 1-cycle use interlock instead of shaving LUTs after the DSP.

title: Rebalance EX: registered wrong-path squash (redirect leaves the ID/EX clear), MUL/DIV results moved to a MEM-stage late select with a 1-cycle use interlock, one-hot AND-OR ALU result
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (r4s1, 93.1-94.2 MHz,
4.49M cycles). Placement option 0 has three path families tied within
0.02 ns at a 10.7 ns data delay (arrival about 16.03 ns, slack -5.74):
  (A) paths 1, 2, 5, 9, 10, 16-25 (37 cells): EX/MEM.alu_result -> EX 1-ahead
      bypass (rs1_1_s1) -> 32-cell carry-chain branch comparator ->
      branch cond / misalign -> redirect -> u_if out.valid -> u_id
      flush -> sync RESET of ID/EX ctrl/rd/valid flops. Redirect is
      still in the ID/EX clear cone through if_stage.out.valid and
      hazard flush_id.
  (B) path 3 (8 cells): ID/EX.op_b_hit -> alu_b bypass -> adder SUM
      (u_alu n90_s2) -> FIVE LUT levels (n705_s18/s10/s4/s1/s0) ->
      EX/MEM.alu_result. That is the 11-way alu_op case mux, then the
      div_done mux, then the mul_sel mux.
  (C) paths 4, 6-8, 11-15 (5 cells): EX/MEM.reg_write (fanout 133) ->
      alu_a bypass -> DSP (3.76 ns) -> 2 LUTs -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
LESSONS r2s0 says to trim every tied path in one iteration: cutting
only one of A/B/C leaves Fmax flat. Every family ends at an EX-owned
result. Rather than tweak each LUT, this change moves work across
pipeline boundaries: the squash of the wrong-path instruction moves one
stage later, and MUL/DIV write their result one stage later.

0.02 ns at a 10.7 ns data delay (arrival about 16.03 ns, slack -5.74):
