hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the fetch store into FOUR banks by pc[3:2] (instead of two by
pc[2]). Every cycle, read the four consecutive words pc, pc+4, pc+8 and
pc+12, one per bank, using only the PC flop. The read at cycle t is for
the word used at t+2, PC(t+2), which is one of pc, pc+4 or pc+8. Those
three are always in three different banks, so the read covers every
no-redirect path, whatever stall_if does in t and t+1. stall_if then
only picks a bank output at t+1, as the last LUT in front of
fword_q / hit_q.

Read (cycle t, PC flop p, j = p[3:2]):
  base  = p[31:4], base1 = p[31:4] + 1   (one short incrementer)
  bank k reads addr a_k = {(k < j) ? base1 : base, k[1:0], 2'b00}
  index_k = a_k[IDX_W+3:4]
The only logic between the PC flop and each BSRAM address is the
incrementer plus a 2:1 mux on a 2-bit constant compare of p[3:2].
No stall, no redirect and no hazard term. The per-bank expected tag
a_k[19:IDX_W+4] and in-range bit (a_k[31:20] == 0) are registered next
to the reads (4 x (TAG_W+1) flops). coll_q <= stall && fill is
unchanged: the hold candidate at t+1 is the bank being filled at t
exactly when stall(t) was 1.

Pick (cycle t+1, current PC flop pc, cur = pc[3:2], nxt = cur + 1):
  hit_k    = rd_k.valid && rd_k.tag == exp_tag_q[k] && inr_q[k]  (parallel)
  hold_w   = rd[cur].word,          seq_w = rd[nxt].word   (4:1 on flop selects)
  hold_h   = hit[cur] && !coll_q,   seq_h = hit[nxt]
  word_d   = stall ? hold_w : seq_w                          (last LUT)
  hit_d    = (stall ? hold_h : seq_h) && !red1_q
This is exact without a redirect: PC(t+1) = stall(t) ? p : p+4 lies in
the window, and so does PC(t+1)+4 <= p+8. With a redirect at t or t+1,
the existing red1_q gating (inside hit_d and in fetch_ok) masks the
result, as it does today. fetch_ok, the ID word mux, the hazard unit's
parallel raw/store rs compares, the fill rule and the synthesis
post-reset sweep keep their current form.

Also grow each bank to 512 entries (IDX_W = 9: 4 x 512 = 2K words,
8 KB, tag = pc[19:13], 7 bits). The entry is 1 + 7 + 32 = 40 bits.
Gowin SDP BSRAM is at most 36 bits wide (512x36), so a 256-deep bank
already needs 2 BSRAMs. The deeper bank therefore costs no extra BSRAM
(8 for the store, 46 on the device). The shorter tag also shortens the
compare on the pick path. Fewer direct-mapped conflict misses on
CoreMark's -O3 hot code (list/matrix/state/crc) can only cut cycles.
The gain is not estimated and is not counted below.

Expected Fmax: the stall_if -> BSRAM-address path is removed rather
than trimmed. The remaining stall_if loads are the PC enable (the same
as the 108.66 MHz base) and one LUT per fword_q / hit_q D pin, which
end at local flops with ordinary setup. The next floor should then be
the 105-108 MHz family that r6s0 / r8s0 / r8s1 measured (EX compare ->
redirect -> PC, dmem -> ID load forward). At unchanged cycles, 100.96
-> ~106-107 MHz gives +5-6%, and conflict-miss savings add to that.
Risk: the pick path is BSRAM clk-to-out -> tag compare -> 4:1 ->
stall LUT -> flop, one MUX2_LUT5 deeper than today's 2:1. Keep stall
as the last select, and keep the 4:1 on flop selects (pc[3:2]) only.

implementation_notes:
# hyp-20260930-001-r10s0 — stall-free fetch-store read address

## What changed

- `cores/bench/rtl/fetch_store.sv` rewritten to 4 banks by pc[3:2]
  (IDX_W = 9: 4 x 512 entries of {valid, tag = pc[19:13], word}, 40 bits).
  - Each bank is a `fetch_bank` submodule instance (same file, generate
    loop over k = 0..3): its own `syn_ramstyle = "block_ram"` array, a
    write always_ff (with the reset clear under FETCH_STORE_RESET =
    VERILATOR / RISCV_FORMAL / FORMAL) and a separate sync-read
    always_ff. The FETCH_STORE_RESET define block moved to file scope so
    both modules see it.
  - Read window pc .. pc+12 from the PC flop only:
    `base1 = pc[31:4] + 1`; bank 0 uses base1 when pc[3:2] != 0, bank 1
    when pc[3], bank 2 when pc[3:2] == 3, bank 3 always pc[31:4]. The
    BSRAM read address is `blk[k][IDX_W-1:0]`. stall, redirect and the
    hazard terms reach no BSRAM pin.
  - Per-bank expected tag (`blk[k][15:IDX_W]`) and in-range bit
    (`blk[k][27:16] == 0`) registered next to the reads. `coll_q <= stall
    && fill` and `red1_q <= redirect || busy` unchanged.
  - Pick: per-bank hit compares in parallel; hold = bank pc[3:2], seq =
    bank pc[3:2]+1 (4:1 on the pc[3:2] flops); `word_d = stall ? hold_w :
    seq_w`, `hit_d = (stall ? hit[cur] && !coll_q : hit[nxt]) && !red1_q`.
    stall is the last select only. fetch_ok unchanged.
  - Fill: `we[k] = busy || (fill && pc[3:2] == k)`, waddr = pc[12:4]; the
    synthesis sweep writes invalid entries into all 4 banks.
- `cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv`: FS_IDX_W already was 9 (synth/sim) and 1
  (formal); only a comment added (4 x 512 / 4 x 2 entries).
- `cores/bench/rtl/core.sv`: header comment only.
- `cores/bench/test/test_fetch_store.py`: new exact cycle model (window
  snapshot before the same-cycle fill, pick of stall ? pc : pc+4, collision
  cancel, 2-cycle redirect mask) that asserts fetch_ok every cycle and the
  store word == mem[pc]. Loops at 0x100 / 0x2104 (aliasing index, different
  tag), 0x108, 0xFFFF0 (crosses the 1 MB boundary, base1 into bit 20) and
  0x100100 (out of range, aliasing 0x100's index/tag bits); random
  mid-loop redirects. Coverage asserts: all 8 (pc[3:2], held/seq) pick
  combinations, >10 window-wrap picks (read at pc[3:2]=3 using base1),
  >10 collision cancels, >10 masked post-redirect cycles.

## Deviations

- None of substance. The banks are a submodule instance each rather
  than four inline arrays (cleaner, one `rd` packed array for the 4:1).
- The hypothesis said "grow each bank to 512 entries"; the r9s1 base
  already had IDX_W = 9 (2 x 512). Now 4 x 512 = 2K words.

## Concerns

- BSRAM count: 40-bit entry x 512 needs 2 BSRAMs per bank -> 8 for the
  store (was 4 with 2 x 41-bit banks).
- Pick path is BSRAM clk-to-out -> 7-bit compare -> 4:1 -> stall LUT ->
  flop, one mux level deeper than before; not measured (see below).

## Local checks

- Verilator lint (fetch_store standalone, default and formal params): clean.
- cocotb: full suite 7/7 pass (test_fetch_store 12k cycles, exact model).
- Formal (`RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`,
  auto-detected nret=1 wrapper_si / checks_si): 53 passed, 0 failed, first
  attempt.
- Cosim (`NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`): passed, 2 ELFs (selftest,
  CoreMark with stalls). Note: plain `make cosim` builds with NRET=2 and
  fails to compile main.cpp for this nret=1 core; that is the harness
  default, not an RTL issue.
- Gowin timing (`make timing TARGET=bench`, place_option 0 only):
  101.642 MHz (r9s1 logged 98.22 on option 0), logic 2545 LUT4, 794 regs,
  BSRAM 12, DSP 2. Top paths: DSP op_a -> EX/MEM.xres (15.13 ns, 6 cells),
  imem_ready -> ID/EX.op_a (7 cells), EX/MEM.alu_result -> ID/EX.squash
  (22 cells), imem_ready -> ID/EX.pc_imm. No fetch-store / stall_if ->
  BSRAM-address path among the reported worst paths. Other seeds not run;
  so the +5-6% is not confirmed. Only about +3.5% was seen on option 0.
lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r10s0 (regression, +4.01%): Splitting the fetch store into 4 banks by pc[3:2] and reading the window pc..pc+12 from the PC flop alone (bank k address = pc[31:4] + (k < pc[3:2]); stall_if only picks the held or the sequential word as the last LUT in front of fword_q/hit_q; coll_q = stall && fill still covers the one read/write collision) removed r9s1's logged worst path, fword_q -> load-use -> stall_if -> bank-index mux -> BSRAM address pins, and option 0 rose from 98.22 to 101.64 MHz with no fetch-store path left in the top list; but 270.85 is only ~105.0 MHz at r9s1's 3.877M cycles (lower if the 2K-word store also cut conflict misses), which is the same 105–106.3 MHz floor that r6s0, r8s0 and r8s1 hit, so it most likely missed the 4.6% acceptance margin (~272.4 needed); feeding a BSRAM address pin from a late stall/hazard net cost ~4% Fmax here, so BSRAM addresses should come from flops only, but once the store is timing-neutral the design is back at the existing EX/ID floor (option-0 top paths: DSP op_a -> EX/MEM.xres, imem_ready -> ID/EX.op_a, and the 22-cell alu_result -> squash redirect), and this diff alone cannot clear the margin, so keep it on a side branch and land it together with a measured cut to one of those paths, checked with `make timing` across the scored seeds.

title: Stall-free fetch-store read: 4 banks by pc[3:2], every bank address from the PC flop only, stall picks on the data side
motivation:
The r9s1 fetch store won on cycles (4.53M -> 3.877M measured) but lost ~7%
Fmax (108.66 -> 100.96 MHz; seeds 98.22 / 100.96 / 100.96). The logged
worst path says exactly where: cpu/u_if/u_fs/fword_q -> u_hazard (lu_fs
rs==rd compare -> load_use -> stall_if) -> u_id -> u_if/u_fs/mem_e BSRAM
address pin, 13 cells / 11 levels, 15.48 ns arrival. The fetch store's
read index is `ev_a/od_a = stall ? {pc, pc+4} : {pc+4, pc+8}`, so the
latest control net in the core (stall_if, built from the fetch word's rs
compare, dmem_ready, div_busy) ends on a Gowin BSRAM address pin, whose
setup time is much larger than a flop's. Before r9s1 the same stall net
only reached flop CEs/Ds (PC, ID/EX) and the design ran 108.66 MHz, so
this one BSRAM endpoint costs ~7% on its own. Removing it keeps all of
r9s1's cycle gain and should give most of that Fmax back.

Measured caveat (`make timing` on the r9s1 champion, placement option 0,
98.22 MHz): the top ~25 paths are four families tied within 0.2 ns
(slack -5.18 .. -5.00): fword_q -> stall -> fetch-store BSRAM address;
EX/MEM.alu_result -> compare chain -> redirect -> PC / red1_q / squash;
stall_gen imem_ready -> IF word mux -> ID op_a/op_b/rs2_val; and
alu_result -> bypass -> DSP -> xres. Every family is ~1 ns slower than
at r5s1 (9.2 ns), so the fetch-store BSRAMs, whose address pins are
currently tied to the stall net that also feeds PC and ID/EX, most
likely pull the PC / ID / EX placement toward themselves. With the
address driven only by the PC flop plus a 9-bit incrementer, the placer
no longer has to put the BSRAMs next to the stall cone, which is the
mechanism that could recover the other families too; if it does not,
the other three families cap the gain, so this is low confidence.
The implementer must run `make timing` and report all scored options.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-bank the fetch store so that no BSRAM address depends on stall (or on
redirect): the late stall decision moves to the data side, one cycle
later, where it drives only the D-mux of fword_q / hit_q (flops), just as
it already does today for the final candidate pick.

Why it works: fword_q at cycle t+2 must hold the word at pc(t+2). Absent
a redirect, pc(t+2) = pc(t) + 4*k with k = !stall(t) + !stall(t+1) in
{0,1,2}. With 4 banks indexed by pc[3:2], the words at pc, pc+4, pc+8
(and pc+12) always sit in 4 different banks, so at cycle t every bank can
read "its" word of that window with an address that is a function of the
PC flop only:
  bank j reads idx_j = pc[12:4] + (j < pc[3:2])     (9-bit, flop-driven)
At t+1 the four registered bank outputs hold pc(t)+{0,4,8,12} and the
wanted word is in bank (pc(t+1)[3:2] + !stall(t+1)) mod 4, where
pc(t+1) is simply the current PC flop. So the pick is
  held = bank[pc[3:2]], next = bank[pc[3:2]+1]   (4:1 on PC flop bits)
  fword_d / hit_d = stall ? held : next           (stall is the last select)
which is the same late-select position stall has in r9s1 (sel_o =
pc[2] ^ !stall), plus one 4:1 level on early flop selects.

Everything else keeps r9s1's exact semantics, so cycle count must be
unchanged (3.877M, or slightly lower from the doubled capacity):
  - Fill: bank pc[3:2], index pc[12:4], data {1, tag, imem_data}, WE =
    imem_ready && pc < 1MB && !busy (all flops / port, as today).
  - Collision: the held slot of the current read is the word being
    written; register coll_q <= fill && stall and cancel the held
    candidate when coll_q && stall (identical to today's rule).
  - Redirect: red1_q and the 2-cycle hit masking stay as they are
    (the reads never used the redirect target anyway).
  - Hazard: lu_fs still compares fword_q rs fields; fetch_ok is still
    imem_ready || (hit_q && !red1_q); the ID word is still the LUT3
    `imem_ready ? io_imemData : fword_q`. No change outside fetch_store
    except the IDX_W parameter plumbing.
Geometry: 4 banks x 512 entries x {valid, tag = pc[19:13] (7b), word}
= 40 bits -> 2 BSRAM blocks per bank, 8 blocks total (r9s1 uses 4 for
the store + 4 for dmem; GW2AR-18 has 46), so capacity doubles to 2K
words for free. The per-bank expected tag / in-range bit is registered
alongside the read (computed from the same flop-only bank address; a
conservative miss when the +1 wraps the 9-bit index across an 8 KB
boundary is acceptable and avoids a tag incrementer). Sweep writes all
4 banks for 512 cycles as today. Under formal FS_IDX_W stays 1
(4 banks x 2 entries).

Expected: the fword_q -> hazard -> stall -> BSRAM-address family
disappears; stall's endpoints become PC / ID/EX / fword_q / hit_q flop
CE/D pins, which is the r5s1-era topology that closed 105-108.66 MHz.
The new post-BSRAM path (BSRAM Q -> 8-bit tag eq -> 4:1 on pc[3:2] ->
2:1 stall / red1 / coll mask -> hit_q) is one 4:1 level longer than
today's BSRAM -> hit_q path, which is not in the top paths; to keep it
short, compute the four per-bank hits in parallel and select held/next
with pc[3:2] before the stall mux (never compare after the mux). At
unchanged cycles, 105-107 MHz is +4..+6% (fitness ~271-276).

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r10s1 (improvement, +5.11%): This is the same stall-free 4-bank fetch-store read that sibling r10s0 built in the same round (every BSRAM address from the PC flop, stall_if only as the last select in front of fword_q/hit_q), and it was accepted at 273.71 (~106 MHz if cycles matched r10s0's measured 3.873M) while r10s0 scored 270.85 at 104.9 MHz, a result the r10s0 lesson had said could not clear the ~4.6% margin; the RTL differs only slightly (a 9-bit index-only `idx + 1` with a conservative per-bank wrap-kill and one shared registered tag/in-range bit, instead of a 28-bit pc[31:4] + 1 with a registered tag per bank), which may have shortened the carry chain on the BSRAM address pins, but a ~1% gap between two builds of one idea is smaller than the 101.6–104.9 MHz spread across placement options that r10s0 logged, so treat single-build scores within ~1% of the margin as noise rather than evidence, keep BSRAM address math at index width with a conservative miss rather than full-width, and expect ~106 MHz to still be the 105–106.3 MHz EX/ID floor (DSP op_a -> xres, imem_ready -> ID/EX.op_a, alu_result -> squash redirect) that the next iteration has to cut.

title: Fetch store as a 1K-entry tagged BTB: fill-time JAL/backward-branch predecode steers PC and store read address from flops
motivation:
On the r9s1 fetch-store champion (~3.877M cycles at 100.96 MHz) a taken
control transfer costs more than the 1 squash bubble it cost before:
every EX redirect also blacks the fetch store out for 2 cycles (red1_q
and hit_q masking, because the store read index excludes the redirect),
so those cycles fall back on the 78%-ready bus. r9s1's own model puts
that blackout at ~144k cycles (3.863M -> 3.719M for the
redirect-indexed variant) over ~357k redirects, i.e. ~0.40 cycles per
redirect, so a redirect now costs ~1.4 cycles. ISS trace (r1s2) of the
timed window: 294,425 taken conditional branches (235,191 of them
backward), 51,941 backward not-taken, 49,367 JAL, 13,735 JALR.

Every earlier predictor lost Fmax to NEW state on the PC nets: same-
cycle predecode of io_imemData in front of the PC (r1s2..r5s2), or a
LUT-RAM BTB indexed by the PC/io_imemAddr flop (r6s2, r7s2, r8s2,
r9s2 all landed at 94-105 MHz with +300 LUT4s). The r9s1 fetch store
already is a 1K-entry, fully tagged, direct-mapped table that is read
one cycle ahead of use and whose output is registered (fword_q /
hit_q). Storing predecode bits in the same entries turns it into a
BTB with no new RAM, no new PC-flop index loads and no new lookup
logic: the prediction for the word at PC arrives as flops in the
same cycle as the word itself. LESSONS (r9s2) says to try a predictor
again only on the fetch-store champion, where redirect bubbles are a
larger share of cycles; this is that attempt, built so that nothing
new is added to the stall_if, redirect or branch-compare nets.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a static (BTFN + JAL) direction/target predecode to every fetch
store entry and use it to steer both the PC and the store's own
one-cycle-ahead read address, so a correctly predicted taken
JAL/backward branch costs 0 bubbles AND no store blackout.

1. Entry format (fetch_store.sv): {valid, tag, word, pt, ptgt[19:2]}
   (41 -> 60 bits; still 2 x 512x36 BSRAM per bank, no new blocks).
   pt = 1 iff the word is a JAL with imm[1]==0, or a legal conditional
   branch (dec_is_branch) with imm[31]==1 (backward) and imm[1]==0,
   and pc+imm is in range (pc_imm[31:20]==0). ptgt = pc_imm[19:2].
   Compute it at fill time from ID's existing decoder outputs and
   ID's existing pc_imm adder (the ID word IS the filled word, see 2),
   so no new adder. Sweep writes pt = 0.
2. Store word priority: when the store hits for PC
   (use_store = hit_q && !red1_q, flops only) IF takes fword_q even if
   the bus is ready, and the fill is skipped (fill = imem_ready &&
   !use_store && in-range && !busy). The ID word mux select, fetch_ok
   and the hazard unit's lu_bus/lu_fs pick change from io_imemReady to
   use_store (a flop LUT2, earlier than the input pin). Content is
   identical in real programs, and it makes every steered word
   self-consistent with its predecode (in formal the symbolic bus word
   can differ from the stored one; with this rule the executed word
   and its pt/ptgt always come from the same entry, so EX never needs
   a target check or a replay path).
3. Prediction output: register BOTH banks' pt/ptgt raw from rd_e/rd_o
   (38 flops, no stall in their D cone) plus sel_q <= sel_o, and pick
   after the flops: pt_s = sel_q ? pt_o_q : pt_e_q, likewise ptgt_s.
   This keeps the stall_if -> sel_o fanout exactly as today (r9s1's
   suspected Fmax loss was stall_if loads; do NOT widen word_d).
   steer = use_store && pt_s.
4. PC (if_stage.sv): pc <= redirect ? redirect_target
                         : !stall ? (steer ? {12'b0,ptgt_s,2'b0} : pc+4)
                         : pc.
   The steer pre-mux is flops -> 2 LUTs, in parallel with the pc+4
   carry chain; redirect stays the last select and CE is unchanged.
5. Store read address: A = stall ? pc : (steer ? ptgt_s : pc+4), with
   A and A+4 split across the banks as today; the steer case needs
   ptgt_s + 4 (an 18-bit incrementer from flops, or computed per bank
   before the pt/ptgt flops). Pre-mux the !stall candidate from flops
   and keep stall as the LAST select on every index/tag/inr bit
   (syn_keep the pre-muxed candidate so Gowin does not re-merge it,
   r9s0). Collision: a steered read can now hit the fill address
   (branch to itself / 2-word loop, ptgt or ptgt+4 == pc); register a
   flop-only compare of ptgt_s vs pc and cancel both candidate hits
   for that cycle (conservative, rare).
6. ID (id_stage.sv): capture pred = steer into ID/EX. Redirect target
   field pc_imm := pred ? pc+4 : pc+imm; cmp_inv := funct3[0] ^ pred;
   jal_ok := JAL && !imm[1] && !pred. br_ok / jal_mis unchanged. Keep
   the true pc+imm in a separate RVFI-only field (pruned by synthesis).
7. EX (ex_stage.sv): the redirect expression, the target mux and the
   compare chain are textually unchanged, so a steered branch that
   falls through redirects to pc+4 through the same 1-LUT tail and a
   steered taken branch / JAL does not redirect. misalign_branch =
   branch_cond && imm[1] stays exact (pred implies imm[1]==0). Only the
   RVFI-only pc_next uses real_taken = branch_cond ^ pred and the true
   target field. No new loads on branch_cond or redirect.

Cycle model: correctly steered = (235,191 backward taken + 49,367 JAL)
x ~0.97 store hit ~= 276k redirects removed at ~1.4 cycles each
(~386k); new wrong steers = 51,941 backward not-taken x 1.4 (~73k);
forward-taken and JALR unchanged. Net ~ -313k cycles, 3.877M -> ~3.56M
(-8.1%, +8.8% fitness at equal Fmax). Every new input to the PC,
index and ID cones is a flop and the stall_if/redirect/branch_cond
fanouts are unchanged, so the Fmax cost should be the ~1-2% of extra
placement (+~150 LUT4, +~60 FF), giving ~ +6-7% net. Measure real
cycles and run `make timing` across the scored seeds; if the fill
data path (io_imemData -> ID decode/pc_imm -> BSRAM din) shows up,
register the fill one cycle (write visible one cycle later) instead of
trimming elsewhere.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r10s2 (regression, -9.09%): Storing static BTFN/JAL predecode (pt, ptgt[19:2]) in the r9s1 fetch-store entries and steering the PC and the store read address from registered pt/ptgt did cut cycles, to a measured 3,605,406 (-7.0%, against the -8.1% model; the gap is a one-cycle st1_q store blackout after every steer, needed because the pick for that cycle is made before the target can be read), but Fmax fell from 100.96 to 85.3 MHz (-15.5%) for only ~+100 LUT4 (2543 vs 2443), a bigger loss than r6s2–r9s2's ~+300-LUT4 BTBs took, so the cause is most likely one new long path rather than general placement growth, and the likeliest is the unregistered fill, where `fill_pt = (JAL || backward branch) && pc_imm[31:20] == 0` and `fill_ptgt = pc_imm[19:2]` run from the io_imemData pin through ID decode and the full 32-bit pc+imm carry chain into the BSRAM write data (both the hypothesis and the implementer flagged this path, but `make timing` was not run); like BSRAM addresses (r10s0), BSRAM write data should come only from flops, so rebuild it on the r10s1 4-bank champion with the predecode written one cycle late from ID/EX flops (the pc+imm range check at index width, as r10s1 did for address math) and accept it only if `make timing` across the scored seeds shows at most ~2.7% Fmax loss, the most a -7.0% cycle cut can absorb and still clear the 4.6% margin.

title: Fetch-store reads the static-taken target window from ID/EX.pc_imm, removing the 2nd post-redirect blackout cycle
motivation:
`make timing` on the r10s1 champion (place option 0, 102.68 MHz) shows at
least seven path families tied within 0.15 ns of the 15.03 ns worst
arrival: alu_result -> bypass -> compare chain -> 3 u_if LUTs ->
squash/PC (32 cells; the carry chain itself is only ~0.9 ns, the rest is
routing), alu_result -> alu_b bypass -> DSP -> xres, dmem BSRAM -> load
align -> ID/EX.op_b, MEM/WB.rd -> regfile write-first bypass ->
ID/EX.op_b, stall_gen lfsr -> imem_ready -> fetch_store hit_q, ID/EX.op_a
-> ALU -> alu_result, and imem_ready -> ID/EX.op_b. r6s0, r8s0, r8s1 and
r9s0 each cut one or two of these and landed at 105-106 MHz, so another
zero-cycle trim is very unlikely to clear the 4.6% margin. This slot
therefore goes after cycles, with only flops feeding any new logic.
The largest cycle cost the fetch store still leaves is after a redirect:
the store's pick is one cycle ahead of use, so after a redirect in
cycle t the words for t+1 and t+2 can come only from the bus (red1_q
and the hit_q fold), and each of those cycles has a 22% imem-stall
chance. r9s1's trace model priced the full redirect-indexed fix (both
cycles, all redirects) at 3.719M vs 3.863M cycles (-3.7%), but it needs
the late redirect_target on the BSRAM address pins, which r10s0 showed
costs ~4% Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove the second blackout cycle (t+2) for statically-taken control
flow without putting a late net on any BSRAM pin. The branch/JAL target
is already an ID/EX flop (ID/EX.pc_imm, added in ID), and whether the
instruction in EX is statically taken is known one cycle early:
ID/EX.pt, a new registered bit set in ID as
`jal_ok || (br_ok && imm[31])` (JAL, or backward branch = BTFN).
The hit mask at t+1 becomes `!(red1_q ^ tsel_q)` (red1_q still includes
busy): hits stay valid when the window matched the PC path (no redirect
and no target read, or a predicted redirect to the target that was
read) and are masked otherwise.
1. id_stage: register `pt` into ID/EX (cleared on bubble with the other
   control fields; the squash kill is applied in fetch_store as below).
2. fetch_store: the per-bank read index/window base becomes
   `tsel ? ID/EX.pc_imm : pc` where tsel = ID/EX.pt && !ID/EX.squash.
   Both data inputs and the select are flops, so each BSRAM address pin
   gets one LUT3 of flops (index width only, per r10s1: the +1 is on
   the 9-bit index with the conservative per-bank wrap-kill); the
   expected tag / in-range bit / kill_q are registered from the same
   selected base. Also register `tsel_q <= tsel`.
3. Pick at t+1: if tsel_q (window = target's) then the candidate for
   t+2 is chosen against the redirected PC (pc(t+1) = target when the
   redirect fired): held = bank[pc[3:2]], next = bank[pc[3:2]+1],
   exactly the existing pick, because pc(t+1) is now inside the window
   that was read. The red1_q term in hit_d is replaced by
   `red1_q && !tsel_q` (a redirect that was predicted keeps its hits;
   an unpredicted redirect - JALR, forward taken branch - still masks).
   fetch_ok at t+1 is unchanged (still bus only after any redirect).
4. If tsel fired but the branch was not taken (loop exit), the window
   read at t is the target's, not pc's, so the candidate for t+2 is
   masked: fold `tsel_q && !red1_q` into the hit_d mask. Cost: one
   22%-stall exposure per mispredicted backward branch, the same
   exposure every taken branch has today.
5. coll_q stays as is (the fill still writes at pc; a same-address
   collision can only happen on the held pick, which is unchanged).
No change to the PC, the redirect cone, the hazard unit, the ID word
mux or any EX path: stall and redirect still reach only the last
select in front of fword_q / hit_q, and the new tsel mux in front of the
BSRAM address comes from flops. Expected cycle cut: each correctly
predicted taken branch/JAL saves the 22% stall exposure of cycle t+2
(~0.22-0.28 cycles incl. repeated stalls); with ~300k statically-taken
redirects in 10 CoreMark iterations and a ~10-15% BTFN loop-exit
penalty, about -1.5% to -2.5% cycles. Fmax should be unchanged within
seed noise because no tied path gains an input; the only new loads are
~9 index bits x 4 banks on ID/EX.pc_imm and the pt/squash flops.
Honest caveat: on its own this is below the 4.6% margin; it is the
flop-only, zero-Fmax-risk half of the redirect-indexed store, and it
is worth scoring only if the implementer confirms with `make timing`
that no fetch_store or ID/EX.pc_imm path moves into the top 10 and
measures the real cycle count with the stall model.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r11s0 (regression, +0.51%): Choosing the fetch-store window base between the PC flop and ID/EX.pc_imm on a registered static-taken bit (tsel = ID/EX.pt && !squash, set for JAL or a backward branch), which removes the second post-redirect store blackout cycle after predicted redirects, kept every BSRAM address pin a LUT3 of flops and did not cost Fmax (place option 0 at 105.52 MHz vs the champion's 102.68, no new logic in the top 5; scored best seed 105.4 vs ~106.0 MHz, within the seed spread), which confirms that a flop-only mux in front of BSRAM addresses is safe; but the measured cycle cut was only -1.07% (3,873,081 -> 3,831,750, ~41k cycles), about half the back-of-envelope -1.5 to -2.5% (~300k predicted redirects x 0.22–0.28 cycles) and under a third of the -3.7% the r9s1 trace model gave the full redirect-indexed store, so most of the remaining blackout cost is most likely in the t+1 cycle and in unpredicted redirects (JALR returns, forward taken branches), which a flop-only base cannot reach; price partial fetch-side variants with the trace model (within ~200 cycles on r9s1) before building them, and because a ~1% cycle trim cannot clear the 4.6% margin by itself, keep this diff on a side branch and land it only together with an orthogonal Fmax or cycle gain.

title: Retire-side fetch-store fill: fill the 4-bank store from ID/EX flops with next-fetch predecode, steer PC from registered store outputs
motivation:
Most of the remaining cycles on the r10s1 champion (3.873M cycles, ~106 MHz)
come from control transfers. The r1s2 ISS trace of the timed window has
294,425 taken conditional branches (235,191 of them backward), 49,367 JAL

   true memory word at its pc, so it may fill):

motivation:
r10s2 is the only predictor that cut cycles by more than its Fmax cost
in the cycle model. Storing static predecode (pt = JAL, or backward
branch; ptgt = target[19:2]) in fetch-store entries cut measured cycles
from 3.877M to 3,605,406 (-7.0%). It then lost 15.5% Fmax
(100.96 -> 85.35 MHz) to one new path. The logged worst path was
red1_q -> u_if word select -> u_id decode -> u_id/u_imm -> pc_imm carry
chain -> u_if/u_fs/mem_o BSRAM write-data pin: 32 cells, 16 levels,
17.48 ns. That is the unregistered fill, which computed
fill_pt/fill_ptgt from the live IF word and wrote them into BSRAM din
in the same cycle. It added only ~100 LUT4 and no new RAM, so the loss
was this one path, not placement growth like the +300-LUT4 BTBs in
r6s2-r9s2. LESSONS (r10s0, r10s2) give the rule: every BSRAM pin
(address, write data, WE) must be driven from flops. The r10s2 lesson
also asks for exactly this rebuild on the r10s1 4-bank champion, where
the store read already comes from flops.

costs ~1.44 cycles: 1 squash bubble plus a 2-cycle store blackout
(red1_q / hit masking), during which fetch falls back on the 78%-ready
bus. The ISS trace of the timed window (r1s2) shows:
  - 235,191 backward taken branches
  - 49,367 JAL
  - 59,234 forward taken branches
  - 51,941 backward not-taken branches
  - 13,735 JALR

~276k redirects into a 1-cycle bus-only blackout (0.22 expected
cycles). The 52k backward not-taken branches become mispredicts at the
same 1.44-cycle cost a redirect has today. Net saving is about
276k x 1.22 - 52k x 1.44 ~= 262k cycles, giving ~3.61M cycles (-6.8%),
in line with r10s2's measured -7.0%.
Clearing the 4.6% margin needs Fmax >= ~103.3 MHz (<= 2.5% loss).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild r10s2's fetch-store predecode steering on the r10s1 4-bank
store. No new cycle path may reach a BSRAM pin, the redirect net or
the branch-compare net. The EX redirect expression and compare chain
stay textually unchanged.

1. Entry format (fetch_store.sv): {valid, tag = pc[19:13], word, pt,
   ptgt[19:2]} = 59 bits. That still fits the 2 x 512x36 BSRAM blocks
   each bank already uses, so no new RAM. Sweep and reset write
   pt = 0.

2. Store-word priority. use_store = hit_q && !red1_q (flops only).
   When the store hits, IF takes fword_q even if the bus is ready.
   This keeps the executed word and its pt/ptgt from the same entry,
   so EX needs no target check or replay, and formal stays sound when
   the symbolic bus word differs. Changes:
     - ID word: use_store ? fword_q : io_imemData.
     - fetch_ok = use_store || imem_ready.
     - hazard pick: use_store ? lu_fs : lu_bus.
   These selects become a flop LUT instead of the io_imemReady pin.

3. Fill written one cycle late, from flops only. This is the fix for
   r10s2's 17.5 ns path.
     - Pulse flop: fwe_q <= !stall_id && imem_ready && !use_store
       && pc_in_range && !busy. That is: ID/EX captured a bus word
       this cycle.
     - Next cycle, the write port takes everything from ID/EX flops:
         bank  = pc[3:2]
         index = pc[12:4]
         tag   = pc[19:13]
         word  = instr (ID/EX.instr becomes live)
         ptgt  = pc_imm[19:2]
         pt    = (jal_ok || (br_ok && imm[31])) && pc_imm[31:20] == 0
       pt is a 12-bit NOR plus 2 LUTs from flops.
     - Nothing from io_imemData, ID decode or an adder reaches din,
       and ID gains no new adder.
     - Collision: kill_q[j] <= wrap_kill || we[j]. Any bank written
       this cycle has its read ignored next cycle. Fills only happen
       while the store misses, so this costs about nothing, and SDP
       read-during-write never matters. The old coll_q
       (fill && stall) goes away.
     - Words stuck in IF during a long stall are filled when they
       advance instead of while they wait. Fill visibility is 3
       cycles instead of 2. Both are minor.

4. Prediction output.
     - Carry pt/ptgt through the existing pick: 4:1 on the PC flop
       bits [3:2], then stall as the LAST 2:1 select, next to
       word_d/hit_d, into pt_q/ptgt_q flops.
     - If stall_if fanout shows up in timing, give the fetch-store
       data selects a syn_keep'd duplicate of stall_if.
     - steer = use_store && pt_q (LUT3 of flops).

5. PC (if_stage.sv):
     pc <= redirect ? redirect_target
         : !stall   ? (steer ? {12'b0, ptgt_q, 2'b0} : pc + 4)
         :            pc
   The steer pre-mux is built from flops in parallel with the +4
   incrementer. Redirect stays the last select and the CE is
   unchanged.

6. Store read address, so a steer costs a 1-cycle blackout instead of
   2. Define the base A = steer ? ptgt_q : pc.
     - Every read-side quantity the champion computes from pc uses A
       instead: idx, idx+1, nxt_j = (j < A[3:2]), tag_q, inr_q
       (= steer || pc[31:20] == 0) and wrap_kill.
     - Only flops (steer terms, ptgt_q, the PC flop) feed the address
       pins: one LUT before the existing 9-bit incrementer.
     - Stall and redirect never reach the address.
   Blackout and mismatch masks:
     - Pick in the steer cycle: hit_d = stall ? hit_h : (hit_n && !steer).
       The next-sequential word is wrong-path.
     - Steer while stalled (PC holds, window read at the target): a flop
       wbad_q <= steer && stall kills hit_d on the following pick.
     - red1_q masking after an EX redirect is unchanged.

   other control flops on a bubble). Only two registered decode bits
   change:
     cmp_inv <= branch_op[0] ^ pred
     jal_ok  <= JAL && !imm[1] && !pred
   br_ok, jal_mis and pc_imm are unchanged. pc_imm stays the true
   target, which the fill also uses.

   textually unchanged. Behavior:
     - A steered branch that falls through redirects.
     - A steered taken branch or a steered JAL does not.
     - misalign_branch stays exact, because pred implies imm[1] == 0.
   Only the non-JALR leg of the target changes:
     t_nj = pred ? in.pc + 4 : in.pc_imm
   t_nj is flops plus an incrementer, ready long before jalr_sum, so
   the late input still passes one LUT3 (is_jalr, jalr_sum, t_nj) in
   front of the PC. The RVFI-only pc_next uses
   real_taken = branch_taken ^ (pred && is_branch) and the true
   pc_imm. It is pruned by synthesis.

BSRAM. If Fmax stays at 103.5-106 MHz, fitness is ~+5-7%.

title: Cut all three tied ~14.6 ns floors in one diff: DSP output register, half-length carry-select branch compare, one-hot load-lane align
motivation:
Fitness = iter/cycle x Fmax, and the r10s1 champion (3.873M cycles,
seeds 102.7/106.0/106.0 MHz) sits on two tied EX paths that every diff
since r6 has landed on (105-106.3 MHz):
  (1) EX/MEM.alu_result -> 1-ahead bypass -> 32-bit compare carry chain
      (the "38-cell compare chain") -> redirect -> ID/EX.squash / PC D
      (champion worst path, 32 cells, 15.03 ns arrival);
  (2) EX/MEM.alu_result -> bypass -> DSP 33x33 -> EX/MEM.xres
      (r11s0 worst path, 6 cells, 14.77 ns).

with a prod_q DSP output register at zero cycle cost, but (1) alone then
held Fmax (its redirect fold was re-structured by Gowin and reverted);
r8s0 cut only the heads and found the compare chain BODY from flops
(rs1_val -> 38 cells -> redirect -> PC) is itself ~14.5 ns. So the
compare chain length is the floor, not its head, and both paths must be
cut in the same diff (r2s0 lesson: trim every tied path in one go).
No cycle cost: this is purely a shorter-logic change.

title: Posted stores: a 1-entry dmem store post slot so a dStalled store no longer freezes the pipeline, stacked with r11s0's flop-only target window
motivation:
The champion (r10s1, 273.71, 3,873,081 cycles, ~106 MHz) runs
2,922,015 instructions between the markers, so ~951k cycles are
overhead: ~357k redirect bubbles, ~144k post-redirect fetch-store
blackout (r9s1 trace model), ~200k load/MUL-use interlocks, and about
240k dmem-stall cycles (every memory op in MEM pays 0.22/0.78 = 0.28
expected cycles, and today ANY memory op, including a store, freezes
IF..EX). Seven timing families are tied within 0.15 ns at the ~106 MHz
floor (r11s0 timing), and every zero-cycle trim since r6 landed at
105-106 MHz, so the next win has to be a cycle cut that adds no logic
to those paths. The dmem-stall bucket is the only large one no
hypothesis has touched. A store does not produce a result, so nothing
architectural has to wait for it: in-order retirement (RVFI) only
needs the write to reach memory before the next memory access does.
r11s0 separately measured a -1.07% cycle cut at neutral Fmax (flop-only
fetch-store window base) that could not clear the margin alone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the dmem request out of the EX/MEM freeze and let a store that
sees io_dmemReady=0 in MEM retire and "post" instead of freezing the
pipeline.
1. Request group: EX/MEM.mem_addr, write_data, mem_width and a new
   wr_req/rd_req pair (store/load && !misalign) get their own clock
   enable req_ce = !(dmem_freeze) && !(post_q && !dmem_ready). The
   mem_addr flop still drives io_dmemAddr directly (CE only, no mux in
   front of the BSRAM address register it is absorbed into), so the
   dmem BSRAM mapping and the AGU -> address path are unchanged.
2. Post: when the store in MEM sees !dmem_ready and post_q = 0, set
   post_q <= 1; the rest of EX/MEM advances and the store retires to
   MEM/WB with its RVFI fields as usual. While post_q, io_dmemWEn is
   driven from the held request group (wr_req & byte mask), and the
   slot clears on the first cycle dmem_ready = 1.
3. Ordering without any address compare: a memory op may not enter
   EX/MEM while post_q && !dmem_ready (ID/EX mem op -> ID/EX and IF
   hold, EX/MEM captures a bubble, the same pattern div_busy already
   uses). If the posted store completes this cycle, the request group
   loads the next op normally, so every load reads memory after every
   older store has been written and cosim/UART/marker order is kept.
4. The pipeline-wide freeze (dmem_freeze = stall_ex_mem/hold_mem_wb)
   becomes !dmem_ready && EX/MEM is a LOAD, or a store while post_q
   (cannot happen by rule 3, kept for safety). Every new control term
   is a flop ANDed with dmem_ready, the same depth as today's
   !dmem_ready && ex_mem_mem_op.
5. Stack r11s0's measured Fmax-neutral fetch-store change in the same
   diff: window base = (ID/EX.pt && !squash) ? ID/EX.pc_imm : pc, a LUT3
   of flops on each BSRAM address pin, pt = JAL || backward branch,
   hit mask red1_q && !tsel_q plus tsel_q && !red1_q (-1.07% cycles,
   105.4-105.5 MHz measured).
Expected: stores are roughly 8% of the dynamic stream (~230k), so
~65k dStall cycles are exposed today and most are hidden (only a store
followed by a memory op in the very next EX slot while the bus is
still stalled pays anything), about -1.5%; plus r11s0's -1.07%; about
-2.5 to -3% cycles at unchanged Fmax. Price the store part with the
r9s1 trace model before building; if it prices below -1%, extend the
slot to 2 entries only if that keeps io_dmemAddr a single flop.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r12s1 (regression, -3.41%): A 1-entry posted-store slot (mem_addr/write_data/width/wr_req/rd_req moved to their own `req_ce = dmem_ready || !(req_wr_q || req_rd_q)`, a store that sees !io_dmemReady retiring out of EX/MEM, and a memory op in ID/EX held behind an EX/MEM bubble while the post is pending) stacked on r11s0's flop-only target window scored 264.37, ~3.9% below r11s0 alone (275.11 at 3,831,750 cycles, 105.4 MHz), so the store half lost more than its whole ceiling (at most ~65k exposed store dStall cycles, <=1.7%): with fitness = 10·MHz/Mcycles that is ~101 MHz at r11s0's cycles, or ~99.7 MHz if the hoped -2.5% landed, most likely because the "flop ANDed with dmem_ready, same depth as today" argument ignored that the new hold (`!dmem_ready && wr_req && ID/EX mem op && !squash`) adds ID/EX inputs to stall_if/stall_id, which since r10s1 is the last select in front of the fetch-store fword_q/hit_q flops, plus a bubble select on the EX/MEM control inputs; because the store share of the dmem-stall bucket is smaller than the ~3% seed spread it cannot pay for any new term in the stall cone, so pair r11s0 with a change that adds no stall/CE logic, and run `make timing` on each half before stacking an unmeasured change on a measured one, since the combined score cannot say which half lost.

title: Stateless fetch-store steer: static JAL/backward-branch target computed from the store word flop, no stored predecode
motivation:
Static JAL/BTFN steering from the fetch store is the only predictor that
has cut cycles a lot on the current front end: r10s2 measured
3.873M -> 3.605M cycles (-7.0%). It failed on two things that both came
from storing predecode (pt, ptgt) in the store entries, not from the
prediction:
  - r10s2 computed pt/ptgt at fill time from io_imemData -> ID decode
    -> pc+imm -> BSRAM write data, and Fmax fell 15% (85.3 MHz).
  - r11s1 and r11s2 moved that fill to ID/EX flops, which puts a
    pipeline register -> store -> PC -> pipeline loop into the design.
    Both timed out in the riscv-formal pc_fwd_ch0 solve.
None of that state is needed. When the store supplies the IF word, the
word is already a flop (fword_q) and so is the PC. Its static
prediction (JAL, or a conditional branch with imm[31] = 1) and its
target pc + imm are therefore a few LUTs plus one adder, all from
flops. That is not the r1s2..r5s2 path, which went from the io_imemData
BSRAM pin through predecode and an adder into the PC.

ISS counts for the timed window (r1s2 trace):
  - 235,191 backward taken branches and 49,367 JALs. Each currently
    costs one EX-redirect bubble.
  - 51,941 backward branches not taken, which this predictor gets
    wrong.
The champion's worst logged path is the EX compare -> redirect -> PC
path (u_ex -> u_if, 32 cells). Nothing here goes onto that path. The
redirect stays the last select into the PC, and the EX redirect
expression and compare chain keep their structure.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a zero-bubble static predict-taken steer in IF. It is used only
when the IF word comes from the fetch store, and the store gains no new
state.

1. Store-word priority (if_stage.sv, hazard_unit.sv, core.sv).
   - use_store = hit_q && !red1_q (flops only).
   - IF word = use_store ? fword_q : io_imemData.
   - fetch_ok = use_store || imem_ready.
   - Load-use pick = use_store ? lu_fs : lu_bus.
   So the steered word is always the executed word. r10s2 did the same
   and passed formal. The bus fill is unchanged: it still writes the
   bus word whenever imem_ready.

2. Steer (fetch_store.sv or if_stage.sv), from flops only.
   - pt = use_store && the fword_q word is JAL, or a legal BRANCH
     (funct3 not 2 or 3) with instr[31] = 1, and imm[1] = 0.
     Register the opcode/funct3/imm[1] part as pt_q next to fword_q,
     through the same stall-last pick, so that steer is a LUT3 of
     flops.
   - tgt = pc + immBJ(fword_q): the full 30-bit sum pc[31:2] +
     imm[31:2]. Pick the B or J immediate with one LUT per bit from
     fword_q[3]. Full width means the target is exact for any PC, so
     there is no range check on the adder carry and no formal
     counterexample at the 1 MB edge.
   - PC <= redirect ? redirect_target
         : !stall  ? (steer ? tgt : pc + 4)
         :           pc
     redirect stays the last select and the PC CE is unchanged.

3. Store read masking. A steer taken at t (steer && !stall) invalidates
   the next two picks, exactly like a redirect:
     red1_q <= redirect || (steer && !stall) || busy
     hit_d  &= !(steer && !stall)
   So a correct steer saves exactly the one EX-redirect bubble and
   keeps today's 2-cycle post-redirect blackout. The BSRAM read address
   stays PC-flop only.

4. Verification without widening the redirect cone (id_stage.sv,
   ex_stage.sv). Capture pred = steer into ID/EX (cleared with the
   control fields) and fold it into the ID-registered selects:
     cmp_inv' = funct3[0] ^ pred
     jal_ok'  = jal_ok && !pred
     pc_imm'  = pc + (pred ? 4 : imm)
   Put that select before the ID adder, not after the carry chain.
   Then the EX redirect is textually unchanged: a steered branch that
   falls through redirects to pc+4, and a correctly steered branch or
   JAL does not redirect, so its successor is not squashed.
   misalign_branch stays exact because pred implies imm[1] = 0. RVFI
   pc_next / branch_target use real_taken = cond' ^ pred and an
   RVFI-only pc + imm, which synthesis prunes.

5. Optional step 2, only if step 1's `make timing` shows at least 1 ns
   of slack on the fword_q -> adder -> PC path:
   - Take the store read base from tgt when steering, at index width
     only: pc[12:2] + imm[12:2], then the existing idx+1 and nxt
     logic, with the steer flop as the last select.
   - Register tag_q and inr_q from tgt.
   - Kill the fill bank's read when steer && fill.
   This drops the blackout to 1 cycle (r10s2's -7% case).

Cycle model:
  - About 250k correct steers from the store (284.5k at ~88% store
    supply) save 1 cycle each.
  - About 46k wrong steers cost 1 bubble plus a blackout, ~1.44 cycles
    each.
  - Net about -183k cycles, 3.873M -> ~3.69M (-4.7%), or about -6.2%
    with step 2.
Logic added: ~40 LUT4 for the adder and predecode, plus 2 flops. No
RAM, no stored state, no new load on stall_if (beyond one red1_q D
pin), redirect or branch_cond.

Formal: the store is unchanged under RISCV_FORMAL (IDX_W = 1). Before
handoff, run pc_fwd_ch0 alone with a ~10 minute timeout. Then run
`make timing` across the scored seeds. Reject the diff if any new
u_if path is within 0.3 ns of the EX redirect path.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r12s2 (regression, +3.35%): Computing the static JAL/backward-branch PC steer from the fetch-store word flop instead of storing predecode (pt_q picked like fword_q, steer = pt_q && hit_q && !red1_q, a full 30-bit pc + immBJ adder from flops into the PC with redirect still the last select, pred folded into ID's cmp_inv/jal_ok/pc_imm so the EX redirect is textually unchanged) fixed both failures of the stored-predecode builds: riscv-formal pc_fwd_ch0 finished in ~10 s against r11s1/r11s2's 30+ minute timeouts, which indicates the solver cost came from stored target state feeding back into the PC rather than from steering itself, and Fmax held at 103.8 MHz (option 0 103.71, no store-word -> PC path in the top list, nearest new path red1_q -> ID pc_imm 0.34 ns under the worst) against r10s2's 85.3; cycles fell to ~3.67M (-5.3%, better than the -4.7% model) with the 2-cycle post-steer blackout kept, but the ~2.1% Fmax cost (106.0 -> 103.8 MHz, +120 LUT4 against the ~40 estimated) left the score ~1.2% short of the 4.6% margin (~286.3 needed), so this is the first predictor whose Fmax cost is close to fitting, and the next attempt should keep this exact diff on a side branch and add only its step 2 (store read base from the steer target at index width, r10s2's measured -7% / 3.605M case, ~288 at 103.8 MHz), which clears the margin only if step 2 costs under ~0.5% Fmax, checked with `make timing` across the scored seeds, rather than redesign the steer.

title: Loss-free fetch-store target window: read ID/EX.pc_imm for every branch/JAL in EX, serve the not-taken case from a held copy of the previous window
motivation:
The champion (r10s1, 273.71, 3,873,081 cycles, ~106 MHz) spends about
144k cycles on the post-redirect fetch-store blackout: after an EX
redirect at cycle t, the store read issued at t used the sequential
window, so the fetch at t+2 must come from the bus (22% stall draw).
r11s0 showed that choosing the store read base between the PC flop and
ID/EX.pc_imm on a registered bit is Fmax-neutral (option 0 105.5 MHz,
no new path in the top list), but it chose by a static BTFN guess, so
a mispredicted guess cost a bus-only fetch in the other direction, and
it measured only -1.07%. Every zero-cycle LUT trim since r6 has landed
in the 104.5-106.8 MHz band, so the next gain has to be cycles that
add no logic to the EX/ID/stall cones.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the target window loss-free, so it can be used for every
non-squashed br_ok/jal_ok in EX, not only predicted-taken ones.

1. Registered select tsel (ID/EX flop, computed in ID): the word
   captured into ID/EX is a branch with an aligned target or a JAL
   (br_ok || jal_ok), and it is not squashed (fold !squash as r11s0
   did). Every bank's read address is a LUT3 of flops:
   tsel ? index(ID/EX.pc_imm)(+1 per bank) : index(pc)(+1 per bank),
   at index width with the r10s1 conservative wrap-kill; the expected
   tag and in-range bit are muxed the same way from flops.
2. Hold the previous window. Add a 4 x 45-bit "prev" register that
   takes the four bank read words (and hit bits) every cycle the store
   read was the sequential window (CE = !tsel_q, a flop). When the
   branch in EX is not taken, the word IF needs next is at most three
   sequential advances past the PC that issued the t-1 read, so it is
   inside the held window [p, p+12]; the pick uses the prev copy when
   tsel_q && !red1_q (both flops), and the fresh target window when
   tsel_q && red1_q. Stall stays the last select in front of
   fword_q/hit_q, as today.
3. JALR keeps today's behavior (its target is not a flop).
4. Correctness guards (required; a same-tag word from outside the
   window would otherwise pass the tag check):
   - Containment: a 2-bit saturating age flop counts PC advances since
     the prev window's read (reset when prev loads, and on redirect).
     Precompute ok_h = age <= 3 and ok_n = age <= 2 from flops and
     let stall pick between them, like hit_h / hit_n. Use prev only
     when the picked word is inside [p, p+12]; otherwise miss.
     Back-to-back branch/JAL (prev is older than one read) then just
     falls back to the bus, as today.
   - Collision: the target read can hit the slot the fill writes
     this cycle. Per bank, register kill_q = we && (raddr == waddr)
     (index-width compare of flops) and mask that bank's hit, the
     same way coll_q covers the held slot today. Also mask the prev
     bank that collided at its own read.
   - Redirect from the tsel instruction always targets pc_imm (br_ok
     / jal_ok exclude misaligned targets), so the fresh window is used
     only when tsel_q && red1_q; a redirect with !tsel_q (JALR) keeps
     today's red1_q blackout.
Keep a side branch of the diff; if formal pc_fwd_ch0 is slow, run it
alone first (r11s0 passed formal with the same store-read-base form,
and no stored state feeds the PC here).

Nothing new reaches the redirect, load-use, stall_if or ID decode
cones: the only new logic is a flop-selected mux on the BSRAM address
pins (the r11s0 form, measured neutral) and a flop-selected 2:1 in the
pick, both inside u_if/u_fs from flops. Estimated cycle cut: the
blackout's t+2 share on ~343k taken branch/JAL redirects (~0.12-0.14
cycles each, ~45k) plus r11s0's gains without its wrong-guess losses,
about -1.5% to -2.5% cycles at neutral Fmax. This is below the 4.6%
margin by itself; its value is as a loss-free, Fmax-neutral cycle
component that can be kept on a side branch and stacked with r12s2's
steer (which measured +3.35% and was ~1.2% short).

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r13s0 (regression, -2.97%): Making r11s0's pc_imm target window loss-free (a 4 x 45-bit prev copy of the last sequential window with a 2-bit age containment check and registered per-bank read/fill collision kills, so the target read serves every unsquashed br_ok/jal_ok and the not-taken case picks from prev) measured 3,813,604 cycles (-1.54% against the champion, the bottom of its -1.5 to -2.5% estimate) but only ~18k cycles fewer than r11s0's static-BTFN guess (3,831,750), so wrong-direction guesses were never much of r11s0's shortfall, while +285 LUT4 / +138 FF over the champion (2792/911 vs 2507/773, +208 LUT4 over r11s0) cut Fmax to 101.3 MHz (98.7 on option 0) with no u_fs path in the top 5, just the existing alu_result -> PC, imem_ready -> ID imm and alu_result -> xres paths all stretched to ~15.42 ns; with r11s0 (+77 LUT4, -0.6%), r12s2 (+120, -2.1%) and r8s0 (+151, -2.2%), this puts the placement cost of logic that stays off every critical cone at roughly 1–2% Fmax per 100 LUT4 on this ~2500-LUT design, so "flops only, no new path in the top list" does not make a change Fmax-neutral: estimate its LUT/FF count too, require at least ~1.5% cycles saved per 100 LUT4 added, and do not spend a wide state copy to recover sub-1% fetch-side cycles.

title: Data-side shadow store: write-through 2K-word BSRAM copy of dmem serves loads under dStall (dmem analog of the fetch store), stacked on r11s0's flop-only fetch window
motivation:
The champion (r10s1, 273.71, 3,873,081 cycles, ~106 MHz) runs 2,922,015
instructions between the markers, so ~951k cycles are overhead: ~357k
redirect bubbles, ~144k post-redirect fetch-store blackout, ~200k
load/MUL-use interlocks and ~240k dmem-stall cycles. Five zero-cycle
EX/ID trims (r6s0, r8s0, r8s1, r9s0, r12s0) all landed in the same
104.5-106.8 MHz band, so Fmax is set by placement and the remaining
lever is cycles. The only structural move that has won on this base was
r9s1: a BSRAM copy of the imem bus that serves the fetch when
io_imemReady=0 (-14.7% cycles). The dmem bus has exactly the same
per-cycle 22% ready draw (main.cpp calls bus_accepts_main() for both
buses every cycle; the read data io_dmemRData is only "valid" when ready)
and nobody has built the data-side analog. Loads are ~20% of the stream
(~585k); each pays p/(1-p) = 0.28 expected stall cycles, ~165k cycles
(4.3%). Posted stores (r12s1) failed because they added new ID/EX terms
to the stall cone; a load shadow adds none of those, only one term to
the existing dmem_stall AND.
Memory layout (bench/programs/link.ld): .data/.bss at 0x20000, stack top
0x30000, rodata in FLASH near the code. A direct-mapped 2K-word store
indexed by addr[12:2] puts .bss (0x20000..) at indexes 0x000.. and the
stack (0x2F000..0x2FFFF) at 0x400..0x7FF, so the CoreMark 2K working set,
its list/matrix/state buffers and the stack frames should not conflict.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. Data shadow store (new rtl/dmem_shadow.sv, instantiated in mem_stage):
   2048 entries x {valid, tag = addr[19:13] (7b), word[31:0]} = 40 bits,
   inferred as sync-read simple-dual-port BSRAM (~3-4 BSRAMs, the device
   has 46, the fetch store uses ~8).
   * Read: the read address is the same AGU value that feeds
     EX/MEM.mem_addr, i.e. the shadow's BSRAM address register is a copy
     of the flop Gowin already absorbs into the dmem BSRAM (read with
     EX's rs1 + imm at the EX/MEM clock edge, enabled with the same
     !stall_ex_mem CE, so a held load keeps reading its own entry).
     In MEM the shadow word, valid and tag come out of the BSRAM.
   * Hit: sh_hit = valid && tag == EX/MEM.mem_addr[19:13] &&
     EX/MEM.mem_addr[31:20] == 0 (in-range bit registered alongside
     mem_addr in EX/MEM, computed in EX from the AGU, not in MEM) &&
     !coll_q. Only loads use it.
   * Use: hazard_unit dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && ex_mem_mem_op &&
     !(ex_mem_load && sh_hit). mem_stage load data = dmem_ready ?
     io_dmemRData : sh_word (one LUT3 in front of the existing load
     align; sh_word goes through the same align). RVFI mem_rdata
     reports the word actually used. io_dmemREn stays asserted as today
     (the bus read is harmless; io_dmemAddr/REn/WEn/WData are unchanged,
     so the timed wrapper and the oob check see the same traffic).
   * Fill (write-through, all from EX/MEM/MEM-side flops or the bus
     word): (a) a load that completes from the bus (dmem_ready &&
     mem_read && in-range) writes {1, tag, io_dmemRData}; (b) a store
     that is accepted (dmem_ready && |dmem_wen && in-range) updates the
     entry: full-word SW writes {1, tag, wdata}; SB/SH use the BSRAM
     byte enables when the entry's tag matches (sh_hit), otherwise they
     invalidate the entry (write valid=0). Byte-enable writes keep the
     32-bit word per-byte; valid/tag are written as a separate 8-bit
     lane with its own WE. This keeps the shadow an exact copy of every
     resident word, so a hit is always the current memory value.
     MMIO (0x1000_0000..) is out of range (addr[31:20] != 0) and never
     filled or hit.
   * Collision: the only same-address read/write is a store/load fill
     in MEM while the next memory op in EX reads the same index; register
     coll_q = fill && (fill index == read index) and cancel that hit
     (the op then just waits for the bus as today), so SDP collision

title: Re-land r12s2's stateless fetch-store steer plus step 2: steered store read base from flops, 1-cycle post-steer blackout
motivation:
r12s2 (stateless static JAL/BTFN steer from the fetch-store word flop)
is the first predictor that passed formal quickly (pc_fwd_ch0 ~10 s)
and kept Fmax close: 103.78 MHz on the median seeds (option 0 103.71,
above the champion's own option-0 102.68), with cycles 3.873M ->
3.668M (-5.3%). It scored 282.89, ~1.2% short of the 286.3 needed.
Its remaining cycle loss is known and measured: it kept the 2-cycle
post-steer store blackout (the store read at the steer cycle is still
indexed by the PC, so the pick for the cycle after the target is also
unusable). r10s2 built the same static steer with a 1-cycle blackout
and measured 3,605,406 cycles. At r12s2's 103.78 MHz that is
10 / 3.605M x 103.78 MHz = 287.9 (+5.2%), and every cycle below that
adds margin. LESSONS (r12s2) says: keep that exact steer and add only
step 2, checked with make timing; do not redesign the steer.
Rejected diffs are not in git, so this is a rebuild of r12s2 from its
log description, with the step-2 read base designed so that no late
net (stall_if, redirect, imem_ready) reaches any BSRAM address pin
(r10s0: that cost ~4% Fmax).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part A, rebuild r12s2 exactly (log hyp-20260930-003-r12s2):
 A1. Store-word priority: use_store = hit_q && !red1_q (flops); IF word
     = use_store ? fword_q : io_imemData; fetch_ok = use_store ||
     imem_ready; load-use pick = use_store ? lu_fs : lu_bus. The bus
     fill is unchanged.
 A2. pt_q (JAL, or legal BRANCH with instr[31]=1, and imm[1]=0) is
     predecoded from the candidate word and registered beside fword_q
     through the same stall-last pick. steer = pt_q && use_store (LUT
     of flops). tgt = pc + immBJ(fword_q), full 30-bit, from flops.
     PC <= redirect ? redirect_target : !stall ? (steer ? tgt : pc+4)
     : pc; redirect stays the last select, PC CE unchanged.
 A3. pred = steer is captured into ID/EX (control-cleared) and folded
     into ID's registered selects: cmp_inv' = funct3[0] ^ pred,
     jal_ok' = jal_ok && !pred, pc_imm' = pc + (pred ? 4 : imm) with
     the select before the ID adder, so the EX redirect expression is
     textually unchanged (steered-not-taken redirects to pc+4). RVFI
     pc_next / branch_taken use real_taken = cond ^ pred and an
     RVFI-only pc + imm (pruned by synthesis).
Part B, step 2 (the new part): the store window read in the steer
cycle is the target's window, so only the cycle right after the steer
is bus-only.
 B1. Read base = steer ? tgt : pc, where steer is the flop-only LUT
     above (NOT qualified by stall or redirect, so no late net reaches
     the BSRAM address). Only index-width bits of tgt go to the BSRAM
     pins (tgt[12:2] = low bits of the same adder), then the existing
     per-bank "idx + (bank < base[3:2])" with the r10s1 conservative
     wrap-kill. To keep the address cone at one carry chain from
     flops, register the already-selected B/J immediate imm_q and
     imm16_q = imm + 16 (index width only) beside fword_q, through
     the same stall-last pick (computed behind the candidate mux, in
     parallel with the existing tag compare). Then the target's index
     and index+1 are two parallel chains from flops,
     (pc[12:2] + imm_q[12:2])[10:2] and (pc[12:2] + imm16_q[12:2])[10:2],
     not an incrementer behind an adder, and each bank's address is
     one LUT level (steer, nxt = bank < tgt[3:2], 4 candidate bits)
     in front of the pin. imm_q also takes the B/J select LUT off
     r12s2's fword_q -> tgt -> PC path. tag_q, inr_q
     and kill_q register from the selected base (full tgt for
     tag/in-range: these are flops, not pins). Register bsel_q = steer.
 B2. Pick at t+1:
     - bsel_q = 0: exactly today's pick (and r12s2's hit_d mask on
       steer && !stall, since a steer taken now needs a window that
       was not read).
     - bsel_q = 1 and the steer was taken (PC moved to tgt, i.e. the
       steer cycle had !stall and no redirect): pc(t+1) = base, so
       today's pick on pc[3:2] is exact; red1_q is NOT set by a taken
       steer any more (r12s2 set it), so t+2 gets a store word.
     - bsel_q = 1 and the steer cycle stalled (PC held): the window
       is the target's but pc(t+1) is not; mask the candidate (hit_d
       = 0) using a registered stall bit (stall_if already feeds the
       coll_q D pin, so this is one more D pin, not a new cone). The
       steer word is still in IF, so the next cycle reads the target
       window again and the steer, when it goes, still has only the
       1-cycle blackout plus one exposure.
     - Redirect still masks two picks through red1_q / hit_q as today.
 B3. Collision: with a target read base the fill (at pc, bank
     pc[3:2]) can land on the same bank and index as the target read
     (different tag, or a self-loop). Register a per-bank kill
     "we && raddr == waddr" into the existing kill_q (a compare into
     a flop only, never into a pin), so SDP read-during-write
     semantics never matter; coll_q keeps covering the held-slot case
     of the PC base.
Cycle model: ~250k correct steers saving 1 bubble, each now also
saving the t+2 stall exposure (~0.22-0.28 cycles), minus stalled-steer
masking; expect ~3.60-3.62M cycles (r10s2 measured 3.605M for this
exact blackout shape). Fitness 287-289 at r12s2's 103.8 MHz, i.e.
+5.0-5.6%. It clears the 4.6% margin only if part B costs <0.5% Fmax,
so the implementer must run `make timing` and check that no
u_if/u_fs -> BSRAM AD path and no fword_q -> tgt -> PC path is within
0.3 ns of the worst path on the scored seeds, and run pc_fwd_ch0
alone under a 10-minute timeout before handoff (formal keeps
IDX_W=1; nothing is stored beyond today's words).

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r13s2 (improvement, +4.95%): After eight predictor builds lost, the first to be accepted came from following the r12s2 lesson exactly, adding one priced change to a measured near-miss: r12s2's stateless steer from the fetch-store word flop was rebuilt as it was, and the only addition was step 2, a store read base `steer ? tgt : pc` whose select is a LUT of flops, never qualified by stall or redirect; imm_q and imm16_q = imm + 16 were registered beside fword_q so the target index and index + 1 are two parallel index-width carry chains from flops instead of an incrementer behind an adder, and the fill-vs-target read collision is a compare into kill_q, never into a pin; the score, 287.27, landed in the hypothesis's predicted 287–289 band, which at fitness = 10·MHz/Mcycles is ~103.6–104.0 MHz at r10s2's measured 3.605–3.62M cycles for the same 1-cycle blackout, so step 2 cost at most ~0.2% Fmax on top of r12s2's 103.8; the recipe that worked here (steer from flops the store already has, no stored target state, BSRAM address mux on a flop-only select, parallel carry chains instead of chained adders) is the one to reuse, but the margin was thin (+4.95% against the 4.6% needed), which by the r10s1 lesson is within single-build noise, and the implementer reported neither cycles nor `make timing`, so measure the new champion's real cycle count and per-seed top paths before building anything on it.

title: M-unit diet: fully registered DSP multiply with a flop-only 1-ahead replay, plus a one-negator divider
motivation:
The champion (r13s2: 287.27, 104.045 MHz median, seeds 102.7/104.0/104.0,
3,621,876 cycles, 2862 LUT4 / 798 FF) logs its worst path as
EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write -> fwd_b -> alu_b 2:1 bypass -> DSP MULT -> EX/MEM.xres
(6 cells, 15.03 ns arrival). The same DSP path was the r12s2 worst path, so it
has been the head of the timing report for two champions in a row. Two
earlier cuts each removed only half of it: r9s0 registered the product
(prod_q) but left the bypass on the DSP inputs, and r8s1 fed the DSP from
ID/EX flops but put a MUL-operand interlock (decode + rs compare) into the
hazard_unit -> stall_if cone, which r12s1/r13s1 later showed costs more Fmax
than it saves. Separately, r13s0 measured that logic which stays off every
critical cone still costs roughly 1-2% Fmax per 100 LUT4 on this design,
and the sequential divider is the biggest block of logic that CoreMark
almost never uses (no DIV/REM in the timed kernels): three 32-bit negators
(|a|, |b|, result fix-up), a 33-bit trial subtractor, raw operand latches
a_q/b_q and 4 x 32-bit muxes, roughly 250 LUT4 and ~200 FF.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take the multiply fully out of the EX combinational cycle and shrink the
divider, with no change to the CoreMark cycle count except rare 1-cycle MUL
replays.

1. DSP from flops only (ex_stage.sv / alu.sv / id_stage.sv). Add dedicated
   33-bit multiplier operand registers mop_a_q / mop_b_q (sign-extension
   bit folded in from the registered mul_sa/mul_sb), loaded with the same
   enable as ID/EX from ID's op_a_d / op_b_d (already 2-ahead forwarded), so
   Gowin can pack them into the DSP input registers. The product goes into
   prod_q (no reset, no mux, EX/MEM enable) so it packs into the DSP output
   register; MEM picks prod_q[63:32] / [31:0] on the registered mul_hi, or
   the divider result, or alu_result (load data still the last select), as
   r9s0 built. The 1-ahead case (a MUL whose operand is the instruction
   directly ahead) must NOT go through the hazard unit: instead, in EX,
   mul_fix = is_mul && (op_a_hit || op_b_hit) && EX/MEM.reg_write &&
   !mul_fix_q && !squash is folded into the existing div_busy output
   (div_busy' = (is_div && !div_done) || mul_fix). mul_fix is an AND of
   flops, exactly like div_busy, so stall_if/stall_id/the fword_q last select
   gain no new cone, only one more flop term in an existing OR. During the
   mul_fix cycle ID/EX holds, EX/MEM takes a bubble (same path as a running
   divide), and mop_a_q/mop_b_q reload from the EX bypass (alu_a/alu_b,
   flop -> LUT4 2:1 -> D pin); mul_fix_q (set for one cycle) lets the MUL
   proceed next cycle. Cost: +1 cycle only for a MUL whose operand is the
   1-ahead ALU result (loads before a MUL already take the load-use bubble,
   so they arrive 2-ahead through ID); expected well under 0.5% of cycles.
   The EX 1-ahead bypass keeps its other consumers unchanged.

2. One-negator divider (divider.sv). Replace the |a|, |b| and fix-up
   negators with a single shared 32-bit `0 - x` unit, time-multiplexed over
   states NEG_A -> NEG_B -> RUN -> FIX (2 extra cycles per divide, which
   CoreMark's timed region essentially never executes). Keep a_q/b_q for
   RVFI and ALTOPS only (they then feed no timed output and are pruned).
   Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS keep RUN at 2 iterations so the total divide
   latency stays inside the liveness window (check the new count against
   the formal depth).

Expected: the DSP path leaves the report entirely (DSP internal only), EX
loses the 64 bypass-mux loads on the DSP inputs, and ~150 LUT4 leave the
divider; at unchanged cycles this is worth ~2-4% Fmax if the r13s0
per-LUT placement cost holds. The known risk is r9s0's finding that the
alu_result -> branch compare -> redirect -> squash/PC path is tied just
below the DSP path; the implementer must run `make timing` on the diff and
report the per-seed top 5, and report the real cycle count.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r14s0 (regression, -6.55%): Putting the DSP fully between flops (33-bit mop_a_q/mop_b_q loaded from ID's op_a_d/op_b_d, prod_q on the output, MEM word pick) and replaying the 1-ahead MUL case through `div_busy |= mul_fix` instead of the hazard unit, in the same diff as a one-shared-negator divider, scored 268.44, which is ~97.2 MHz at the champion's 3.62M cycles (~97.7 MHz even if the replays added 0.5%), so removing the champion's logged worst path outright cost ~6.5% Fmax, far below r12s0's ~2% band for earlier EX trims; the most likely reason is that "one more AND of flops in an existing OR" is not free on LUT4: the champion's div_busy already has 5 flop inputs (is_div, squash, 3-bit state == S_DONE), and mul_fix adds is_mul, mul_hit, EX/MEM.reg_write and mul_fix_q, so the signal gains a LUT level and now drives a 66-bit mop reload select on top of stall_if (the fword_q/hit_q last select), stall_id and the EX/MEM valid/reg_write, while the mop flops add 66 loads and a 2:1 on ID's op_a_d/op_b_d, the tail of the imem_ready -> ID path that r12s0 saw in the top list; after r12s1 and r13s1 this is the third build to lose more than its ceiling by widening the stall cone, so count a new stall source by the LUT4 inputs it adds to stall_if (it has to arrive as one precomputed flop or stay out), treat the DSP path as closed like the other EX trims, and because nobody reported `make timing`, cycles or LUT counts, the loss cannot be split between the MUL and divider halves.

title: Flop-only stall cone: move the load/MUL-use interlock from ID to EX (consumer enters ID/EX, holds one cycle in EX, operand refreshed from mem_result)
motivation:
Champion r13s2: 287.27 at 104.045 MHz, 3,621,876 cycles, 2862 LUT4.
The only stall term that is still not a function of flops is the
load/MUL-use hazard: io_imemData (imem BSRAM clk-to-out) or fword_q
-> rs1/rs2 == ID/EX.rd compare -> load_use_hazard -> stall_if /
stall_id / flush_id. That one net fans out to the PC CE (32, also
io_imemAddr), the fetch-store last select in front of fword_q /
hit_q / pt_q / imm_q / imm16_q (~60 flops, since r10s1 stall is the
last select there), the whole ID/EX CE (~250 flops) and the ID/EX
control clear. r7s0/r7s1/r12s1/r13s1 all lost because a term they
added entered this cone; the cone itself has never been removed.
Five zero-cycle EX trims (r6s0, r8s0, r8s1, r9s0, r12s0) all landed
in the 104-106 MHz band because they cut path heads while the
high-fanout stall net kept every flop's CE late and every placement
pulled toward the imem BSRAM. Taking the hazard compare out of the
CE cone is a topology change, not a LUT trim: after it, stall_if /
stall_id / the fetch-store pick select are LUTs of flops only
(lu_q, imem_ready, use_store, dmem_ready, EX/MEM mem op, div_busy).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Resolve the 1-ahead LOAD / MUL* / DIV* use hazard in EX instead of ID,
with the same cycle count as today:
  - ID never stalls for load-use. The consumer C is captured into
    ID/EX normally (its rs1_hit_ex / rs2_hit_ex flops already record
    that the instruction then in ID/EX writes its source).
  - lu_q = ID/EX.late_ahead && (rs1_hit_ex || rs2_hit_ex), where
    late_ahead is a new ID/EX flop = (ID/EX.late of the producer,
    unsquashed) registered when C is captured; computed at capture
    from the same compares that feed rs?_hit_ex, so it is a flop.
  - In the cycle C sits in EX with lu_q = 1 (producer now in MEM):
    EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid / reg_write / mem_* cleared, the
    same gate as div_busy), the divider does not start, redirect is
    masked (C's branch compare would read a stale operand), IF and
    the fetch store hold (stall_if |= lu_q), and ID/EX holds every
    field except rs1_val / rs2_val / op_a / op_b, which re-capture
    the producer's value from mem_result for the operand that hit
    (the MEM-stage 2-ahead value ID already forwards). lu_q clears
    itself the next cycle (it is set only on capture).
  - Next cycle C executes with fully resolved operands: exactly the
    timing of today's ID bubble (C executes 2 cycles after the
    producer), so cycles are unchanged (~3.62M), but the refresh mux
    keeps mem_result as the last select in front of each operand
    flop (sel = lu_q ? hit : fwd_mem_rs?), same depth as today.
  - dmem stall during the lu_q cycle: the whole pipeline holds as
    today (stall_ex_mem), lu_q holds with ID/EX, and the refresh is
    only enabled when !dmem_stall (mem_result valid).
Result: hazard_unit loses its io_imemData / fword_q inputs; the PC,
fetch-store pick and ID/EX CEs see only flops; the 10 rs compares
that remain run into the rs?_hit_ex / late_ahead D pins (one LUT
deep, as today). Expected: Fmax 104 -> ~109-111 MHz from the removed
~340-load late CE net and the freed placement pull at the imem BSRAM,
with LUT4 roughly flat (the hazard compare LUTs are replaced by the
refresh-select term). Risk: like r8s0, a cut whose placement benefit
is smaller than the seed spread; run `make timing` across the scored
seeds before handoff and report the top 5 per seed.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r14s1 (regression, -6.20%): Taking the last non-flop term out of the stall cone (the load/MUL-use rs compare on io_imemData / fword_q) by capturing the consumer into ID/EX with a registered lu bit merged into squash, then holding ID/EX one cycle while rs1_val/rs2_val/op_a/op_b re-capture mem_result, scored 269.46, which is ~97.6 MHz at the champion's unchanged 3.62M cycles against 104.0, so removing a cone that was never in the champion's logged top 5 (headed by the EX/MEM.reg_write -> bypass -> DSP path) gained nothing, while the replacement most likely cost the ~6%: the hold-or-refresh select per operand (`lu ? (hit ? mem_result : Q) : ID value`, gated by !dmem_stall) adds a LUT level or CE term on the 128 ID/EX operand flops at the tail of the imem_ready -> ID word -> op_a path; same-round r14s0, whose one change in common was also a new select in front of ID's op_a/op_b (the mop reload), landed at the same ~97.2–97.6 MHz, which marks the ID/EX operand D/CE inputs as a near-critical cone where any added mux costs ~6%, so leave those flops' D and CE logic untouched, treat the ID load-use interlock as settled, and stop funding cuts argued from "fanout / placement pull" that no `make timing` report shows (again none was run).

title: Bank-aligned 64-entry BTFN-disagree bimodal BHT on the stateless fetch-store steer (direction only, targets stay stateless)
motivation:
The r13s2 champion (287.27, ~103.8 MHz, ~3.605M cycles) steers the PC
from the fetch-store word flop with a STATIC direction: JAL and
backward branches are predicted taken, forward branches not taken. On
the r1s2 ISS trace of the timed window that direction rule is wrong
111,175 times (59,234 forward-taken + 51,941 backward-not-taken of
529,588 conditional branches). A 64-entry BTFN-seeded bimodal table
on the same trace cuts that to 46,325 (the r1s2 simulation; 256 entries
only reach 39,609, so 64 is the knee).
In the current front end each of those mispredicts is expensive:
  - forward taken, not steered: EX redirect = 1 bubble + 2-cycle
    store blackout (~0.22 exposed per blackout cycle) ~= 1.44 cycles;
    a correct steer costs only the 1-cycle post-steer blackout
    (~0.22), so each fixed one saves ~1.22 cycles;
  - backward not taken, wrongly steered: the target word is squashed
    and EX redirects to pc+4 = 1 bubble + 2-cycle blackout ~= 1.44
    cycles; not steering costs 0.
The BHT only acts when the IF word comes from the store (the only case
the steer acts on today, ~85-88% of branch words), so the expected cut
is ~64.9k x ~0.87 x ~1.33 ~= 75k cycles (3.605M -> ~3.53M, -2.1%).
Every earlier BHT/BTB lost Fmax because new state sat on the PC /
io_imemAddr nets or on same-cycle io_imemData predecode (r1s2..r9s2),
and stored TARGET state feeding the PC broke formal (r11s1/r11s2).
This design adds neither: the targets stay stateless (pc + imm from
fword_q, exactly as r13s2), the table is read in lockstep with the
store banks from the same flop-only read address and registered like
the BSRAM output, the direction bit joins the existing pt predecode in
front of the pt_q flop, and training is written from EX/MEM flops.
The EX redirect is textually unchanged (pred is already folded into
cmp_inv / jal_ok / pc_imm in ID for any branch, forward or backward).
