hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 2-bit "disagree with BTFN" bimodal counter per word address
pc[7:2] (64 entries), split into 4 banks by pc[3:2] exactly like the
fetch-store BSRAM banks, and use its high bit to flip the static pt of
a conditional branch. Nothing else in the steer changes.

1. fetch_store.sv - table and read (no new PC-net loads):
   - Per bank j: (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)
     logic [1:0] bht [0:2**BHT_W-1], BHT_W = min(IDX_W, 4) (4 -> 16
     entries per bank = one RAM16SDP4 per bank; 1 under formal).
   - Read index = raddr[BHT_W-1:0] of that bank (raddr is already the
     flop-only LUT "steer ? tidx : idx(+1)", and bank j's raddr low 4
     bits are word-address bits [7:4] of the window word in bank j),
     registered as ctr_rd[j] <= bht[raddr_low] in the same always_ff as
     rd. So the counter for every window word arrives as a flop in the
     same cycle as word_b[j], for the PC window and for the step-2
     steer-target window alike. If the extra load on raddr shows in
     timing, give the LUT-RAM its own syn_keep copy of the 4 low
     raddr bits (4 LUT/bank) instead of sharing the BSRAM pin nets.
   - Encoding (zero = weakly agree so the existing sweep / reset
     initialise it): s[1] = predict "disagree with BTFN";
     00 weak-agree, 01 strong-agree, 10 weak-disagree,
     11 strong-disagree. On outcome agree: 00->01, 01->01, 10->00,
     11->10; on disagree: 00->10, 01->00, 10->11, 11->11.
   - pt_of(w, s) = (is_jal && !w[21]) ||
                   (is_br && (w[31] ^ s[1]) && !w[8]).
     ctr_h = ctr_rd[sel_h], ctr_n = ctr_rd[sel_n]; pt_h/pt_n use them;
     stall stays the last select into pt_q. Also register
     ctr_q <= stall ? ctr_h : ctr_n beside pt_q (2 FF) and export it.
     The forward-taken steer needs nothing new: tgt = pc + imm_q is
     already a full signed 30-bit sum and the step-2 target window /
     imm16_q chains are already signed.
   - Write port (all inputs flops, from EX/MEM, see 3): bank =
     waddr[1:0], index = waddr[BHT_W+1:2]. The existing synthesis sweep
     (busy) also writes 2'b00 at sweep_idx[BHT_W-1:0] into every bank
     (16 cycles suffice; it runs 512); FETCH_STORE_RESET clears the
     table on reset like the BSRAM model. A read of the slot being
     written may return old or new data: a predictor-only effect, EX
     verifies every steer, so no kill is needed.
2. core_pkg.sv / if_stage.sv / id_stage.sv - carry the counter:
   if_id_t gets bctr[1:0] (= ctr_q) and bv (= use_store, flop: the
   counter is only meaningful for a store word). id_ex_t gets bctr and
   bv; bv is cleared with the other control fields on flush / !valid
   (data-style bctr is not cleared). No change to pred, cmp_inv, jal_ok
   or pc_imm logic: a forward branch with s[1] = 1 simply arrives with
   pred = 1 and is handled by the existing fold (redirect to pc+4 only
   if it falls through).
3. ex_stage.sv / core_pkg.sv - training from flops, 1 cycle late:
   EX/MEM gets bht_upd = in.ctrl.is_branch && in.br_ok && in.bv &&
   in.valid && !in.squash, bctr, btfn = in.imm[31], and uses the
   existing EX/MEM.branch_taken (real outcome = branch_cond ^ pred,
   today RVFI-only) and EX/MEM.pc[7:2] (today RVFI-only). A branch
   never has a memory op, so an EX/MEM entry holding it is never held
   by dmem_stall and bht_upd writes exactly once. In the next cycle
   fetch_store writes bht[pc[7:2]] <= next(bctr, branch_taken ^ btfn)
   with we = EX/MEM.bht_upd: a LUT of 4 flops for the data, flops for
   the address. branch_cond gains exactly one D-pin load (the
   branch_taken flop), not the ~35 that r9s2 added.
4. Nothing touches stall_if, redirect, the PC mux, the BSRAM address
   pins, the ID word mux or the hazard unit.

Cost: 4 RAM16SDP4 + ~30-40 LUT4 + ~20 FF (un-pruned EX/MEM pc[7:2] and
branch_taken, bctr/bv through ID/EX and EX/MEM, ctr_rd x4, ctr_q).
By the r13s0 rule (~1-2% Fmax per 100 LUT4 of off-path logic) that is
~0.4-0.8% Fmax, against ~2.1% fewer cycles: net ~+1.3-1.7% (fitness
~291-292). This is below the 4.6% margin on its own, so it is the
priced predictor half to stack with an orthogonal gain; it is the
only predictor lever left on this front end worth more than ~0.5%
(JALR returns are 13.7k, ~0.5% even with a perfect RAS, and a RAS is
stored target state that re-opens the r11 formal risk).

Checks before handoff:
 - riscv-formal pc_fwd_ch0 alone under a 10-minute timeout (r1s2..r5s2
   BHTs passed formal; direction state is not the stored-target loop
   that timed out r11s1/r11s2). If it is slow, under RISCV_FORMAL tie
   the counter read to 2'b00 (pure BTFN, r13s2's proven steer): EX
   verifies any pred value, so correctness does not depend on it.
 - Report real cycles (expect 3.52-3.55M) and `make timing` across the
   scored seeds; reject if any u_fs -> pt_q/ctr_q, u_fs BHT or
   EX -> branch_taken path is within 0.3 ns of the worst path.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r14s2 (regression, -7.41%): A direction-only 64-entry "disagree with BTFN" bimodal table on the r13s2 stateless steer (4 x 16-entry LUT-RAM banks read from each fetch-store bank's existing flop-only raddr and registered beside rd, the counter's high bit XORed into the static pt predecode ahead of pt_q, trained one cycle late from EX/MEM flops, no new PC/io_imemAddr load and no stored target) scored 265.99, which is ~96.3 MHz at the champion's 3.62M cycles, or ~94.3 MHz if the predicted -2.1% cycle cut landed, against 104.0 MHz, so ~4 LUT-RAMs and an estimated ~30–40 LUT4 cost 7–9% Fmax, several times the r13s0 rule of 1–2% per 100 LUT4, most likely because all of it sits inside u_fs, on the raddr nets that drive the BSRAM address pins and on the BSRAM rd -> word pick -> predecode -> pt_q path, a region that same-round r14s0's logged worst path (u_fs/hit_q -> ID) shows has no slack left on this base; price any change in or next to the fetch store as a near-critical-path change rather than per LUT, and because direction prediction here has a <=2.1% cycle ceiling (below the ~3% seed spread and half the 4.6% margin), retire it on this front end unless it adds nothing to u_fs, and report real cycles and `make timing` (again not reported) before queuing any fetch-store change.

title: DSP tail to one LUT3: divider result read in MEM from its own flop, divider slimmed
motivation:
The champion's (r13s2, 104.045 MHz, 3,621,876 cycles) logged worst path on
the best seeds is EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write -> 1-ahead bypass select -> DSP ->
EX/MEM.xres (6 cells, 15.03 ns arrival). The xres D input today is
`div_done ? div_result : (mul_hi ? prod[63:32] : prod[31:0])`: five
inputs per bit, so Gowin needs a LUT4 plus a MUX2_LUT5 (or two LUTs)
behind the DSP, and div_done is a 3-bit state compare that fans out to
32 xres bits. The divider also carries ~100 flops that only exist for
RVFI or for a separate result register (a_q, b_q, result_q) and three
separate 32-bit negators, all adding area to a design where r13s0
measured ~1-2% Fmax per 100 LUT4 of placement cost.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's (r13s2, 104.045 MHz, 3,621,876 cycles) logged worst path on
the best seeds is EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write -> 1-ahead bypass select -> DSP ->
EX/MEM.xres (6 cells, 15.03 ns arrival). The xres D input today is
`div_done ? div_result : (mul_hi ? prod[63:32] : prod[31:0])`: five
inputs per bit, so Gowin needs a LUT4 plus a MUX2_LUT5 (or two LUTs)
behind the DSP, and div_done is a 3-bit state compare that fans out to
32 xres bits. The divider also carries ~100 flops that only exist for
RVFI or for a separate result register (a_q, b_q, result_q) and three
separate 32-bit negators, all adding area to a design where r13s0
measured ~1-2% Fmax per 100 LUT4 of placement cost.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the DSP tail a single LUT3 and shrink the divider, without adding a
term to any stall, CE, redirect or ID/EX operand cone:
1. ex_stage: EX/MEM.xres <= alu_mul_out only (LUT3: mul_hi ? hi : lo).
   Add a registered EX/MEM bit `is_divres` (= div_done, captured with the
   rest of EX/MEM). mem_stage picks
     mem_result = mem_to_reg ? load_data
                : res_late ? (is_divres ? div_q : xres) : alu_result
   where div_q is the divider's result flop. Every input of the non-load
   leg is a flop, so load data stays the last select and the MEM -> ID
   forward path does not lengthen. The divider result stays valid for the
   cycle the DIV* sits in MEM: a following DIV* can only overwrite it at
   the end of its own first EX cycle, which is that same cycle.
2. divider: latch raw a into quo_q and b into dvs_q at start, plus the two
   sign flags from a[31]/b[31]; take |a| and |b| in place through ONE
   shared 32-bit negator (ABS_A, ABS_B cycles), and let FIX write the
   signed result back into quo_q through the same negator, so result =
   quo_q and result_q disappears. a_q/b_q remain only for RVFI
   rs1/rs2_rdata and are pruned by synthesis. b == 0 is checked on dvs_q
   in ABS_B. Cost: +1 cycle per divide (CoreMark's timed window has
   essentially none). ALTOPS: keep the same stand-in formulas on the
   RVFI-only a_q/b_q copies (written into quo_q in FIX) so the formal
   spec match is unchanged.
Net: one LUT level (and the div_done fanout) off the champion's worst
path, ~96 fewer flops and ~60 fewer LUT/ALU cells in EX, no cycle change.

title: Write the regfile from MEM, not WB: drop the write-first bypass from the ID read path (MEM/WB becomes RVFI-only)
motivation:
Champion r13s2: 287.27 at 104.045 MHz, 3,621,876 cycles, 2862 LUT4.
Five zero-cycle EX trims (r6s0, r8s0, r8s1, r9s0, r12s0) and three
stall-cone changes (r12s1, r13s1, r14s0/r14s1) all landed at or below
the ~104-106 MHz floor. LESSONS r13s0 puts the placement cost at about
1-2% Fmax per 100 LUT4 on this design, and LESSONS r12s0/r10s0 name
a path that no diff has touched: fetch word (io_imemData / fword_q)
-> rs address -> LUT-RAM regfile read -> write-first bypass -> 2-ahead
mem_result forward / operand pre-select -> ID/EX rs?_val / op_a / op_b.
r14s1 showed that adding a mux in front of those ID/EX operand flops
costs ~6%, so this cone is near-critical. The opposite move, removing
a whole LUT level from it, has never been tried.
The write-first bypass exists only because the regfile is written
from MEM/WB, one stage after the ID-side 2-ahead forward already sees
the final result (mem_result). If the regfile is written at the edge
where an instruction leaves MEM, the 3-ahead instruction is already in
the LUT-RAM when ID reads (sync write, async read), so the bypass,
its two 5-bit compares and the w_en qualification disappear from both
read ports. That is a structural removal (the WB stage stops doing
anything timed; MEM/WB is kept only for RVFI and is pruned by
synthesis), with zero cycle cost: no hazard, interlock, stall or
forwarding rule changes.
This is not r2s1: r2s1 dropped MEM/WB but kept the write-first
bypass, so dmem -> load align -> bypass -> operand landed in one
cycle. Here the write is synchronous at the MEM edge and there is no
bypass at all; the ID-side 2-ahead forward (r4s1) already covers
the in-MEM instruction, which r2s1's base did not have.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the regfile write port from WB to MEM:
  w_en   = EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write (post misalign trap, i.e. mem_fwd_en)
           && EX/MEM.valid && !dmem_stall
  w_addr = EX/MEM.rd
  w_data = mem_result (the same net that feeds ID's 2-ahead forward)
dmem_stall only exists for memory ops in EX/MEM, and EX/MEM holds only
on dmem_stall, so every instruction is in a non-held MEM cycle exactly
once and is written exactly once; a load writes on the edge the bus
delivers. Correctness of ID reads (ID captures only when the whole
pipeline advances): 1-ahead is bypassed in EX from EX/MEM.alu_result
(unchanged), 2-ahead is forwarded in ID from mem_result (unchanged),
and 3-ahead and older have already left MEM, so they are in the
LUT-RAM. The reg_file loses its write-first bypass; the read is
regs[rs] directly. x0: writes to x0 stay blocked; the read keeps the
rs == 0 force only if it can be folded without adding a level, else
rely on regs[0] never being written (cleared by reset under
VERILATOR/RISCV_FORMAL/FORMAL, zero-initialised LUT-RAM in synthesis;
add an explicit zero init for the synthesis branch).
RVFI is unchanged: retirement stays at MEM/WB, rd_wdata = MEM/WB.wb_data
(= mem_result captured), so formal order/reg checks see the same trace.
Timing effect: the ID read cone (fetch word -> LUT-RAM -> ID/EX)
loses one LUT4 level per operand bit, and ~70-90 LUT4 (2 x 32 bypass
LUTs, compares, w_en gating) plus 32 real MEM/WB.wb_data flops leave
the placed design. New load: mem_result drives the LUT-RAM WD pins
(4 per bit for 2 read ports x 2 halves) instead of one MEM/WB flop,
and w_en uses dmem_ready (a pin) plus EX/MEM flops; the WD/WRE setup
of RAM16SDP4 is flop-like, so the MEM path depth is unchanged
(dmem BSRAM -> load align -> mem_result select last -> pin).
Expected: cycles unchanged at ~3.622M; Fmax +2..5% (one fewer level on
a named floor path, ~100 LUT4 / 32 FF less). The implementer must run
`make timing` and report per-seed Fmax, LUT4/FF and the top paths; if
mem_result -> regfile WD shows up in the top list, register only
w_en/w_addr (they are already flops) and keep w_data from mem_result.

title: Steer-cycle bus prefetch: fetch the steer target on the idle imem bus so the 1-cycle post-steer blackout mostly disappears (no new state)
motivation:
The r13s2 champion (287.27; 3,621,876 cycles at 104.05 MHz; 2,922,016
instructions in the timed window) steers the PC from the fetch-store
word flop. The only systematic cost left in a correct steer is the
1-cycle post-steer blackout. At t+1 the PC is tgt, but fword_q was
picked from the window read at base pc, so hit_n is masked and the
word at tgt has to come from the bus, which is ready only 78% of the
time. There are about 284k predicted-taken transfers (235,191 backward
taken + 49,367 JAL), and roughly 87% of them come from the store, so
this costs ~284k x 0.87 x 0.22 = ~54k cycles (~1.5%).
In the steer cycle t itself the bus does nothing useful. The IF word
is fword_q (use_store has priority), and the bus word at pc only
refills a word that is already resident. Previous lessons retired
every other predictor lever on this base: BTB and BHT state near u_fs
or the PC nets cost 7-12% Fmax (r6s2..r9s2, r14s2), stored target
state broke formal (r11s1, r11s2), and JALR is only 13.7k returns.
Putting the wasted bus slot to work is the one predictor-side cycle
saving left that adds no state, no stored target, no new stall or
redirect term, and no BSRAM address logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
In a steer cycle, point the imem bus at the steer target and capture
the returned word as the store word for t+1.

1. Fetch address (if_stage.sv): io_imemAddr = steer ? {12'b0, tgt[19:0]}
   : pc. steer and tgt already exist and come only from flops (pt_q,
   hit_q, red1_q, the pc + imm_q adder). This is the same shape as the
   store's BSRAM raddr (`steer ? tidx : idx`), which r13s2 timed at
   ~0.2% cost. Zeroing the top 12 bits keeps a wrong-path garbage steer
   that the same-cycle redirect overrides from ever putting an
   out-of-range fetch on the bus (invariant 6). A real out-of-range
   target would already be fetched by the champion one cycle later.
   The PC register and its D mux are unchanged, and redirect stays the
   last select.
2. Fill gate (fetch_store.sv): fill = imem_ready && pc in range && !busy
   && !steer. In a steer cycle the bus word is not the word at pc, so
   it must not be written at index(pc). kill_q / fwe follow from fill.
3. Pick (fetch_store.sv): on the non-stall leg, steer (a flop-only LUT)
   selects the bus word instead of the masked sequential pick. stall
   stays the LAST select:
     word_d = stall ? word_h : (steer ? imem_data : word_n)
     hit_d  = stall ? (hit_h && inr_q && !red1_q && !blk)
                    : (steer ? imem_ready
                             : (hit_n && inr_q && !red1_q && !blk))
     pt_d   = stall ? pt_h : (pt_n && !steer)   (step 1: a prefetched
                                                 word never steers,
                                                 same as today's bus word)
   imm_q / imm16_q keep their current D (don't-care when pt_q = 0).
   If the steer stalls, the held pick keeps the branch word, the bus
   word is dropped, and the prefetch repeats next cycle. If a redirect
   fires at t, red1_q masks use_store at t+1 exactly as today.
   At t+1 the PC is tgt, use_store = 1 (fword_q = word(tgt)), and the
   window read at t with base tgt serves tgt+4 for t+2 through the
   existing bsel_q / tag_q / inr_q path, so a correct steer now costs
   0.22 x 0.22 = 0.05 cycles instead of 0.22.
4. Optional step 2, only if make timing shows u_fs slack: predecode
   the prefetched word (pt_of / imm_of / +16 on imem_data before the
   stall select) so that a steer target which is itself a JAL or a
   backward branch can steer at t+1 (chained steer, e.g. a loop-entry
   `j .Lcond` onto a backward branch). The champion cannot do this.
Expected: ~42-50k fewer cycles (3.62M -> ~3.575M, about -1.2 to -1.4%)
for about +65 LUT4 (32 on the fetch address, 33 on the pick), and no
new FF, stall, redirect or BSRAM address term. Formal risk is low:
riscv-formal drives io_imemData freely and no stored target reaches
the PC. The implementer must report real cycles, LUT4 and
`make timing` across all scored seeds. If u_fs/hit_q -> ID or the
pick -> fword_q path moves up, drop step 4 first.
Caveat: on its own this is about +1% and will not clear the 4.6%
margin. It is a zero-state predictor-side gain meant to be stacked
with an orthogonal Fmax or cycle change, not a standalone win.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r15s2 (regression, -2.48%): Recovering r13s2's 1-cycle post-steer blackout by pointing the imem bus at the steer target (imem_addr = steer ? {12'b0, tgt[19:0]} : pc) and picking the bus word into fword_q on the non-stall leg (hit_d gains imem_ready && tinr, word_d a 32-bit steer_pf ? imem_data : word_n mux, plus pt_d, a duplicate pf_q flop and a !steer_pf term on the BSRAM fill enable) scored 280.14, which is at most ~101.5 MHz at the champion's 3.62M cycles (~100.2 MHz if the predicted ~45k-cycle cut landed; a prefetch cannot add cycles) against 104.05, so ~65 LUT4 of "zero-state" logic cost 2.5–3.7% Fmax, about twice the whole blackout bucket (~54k cycles, ~1.5%); in the Fmax build (fpga/core_bench.sv) io_imemAddr only feeds the led XOR and io_imemData is an LFSR flop, so the new fetch-address mux was not the cost, which puts it on the terms added to u_fs's hit_d/word_d/pt_d pick and fill enable (most likely tgt's full carry chain -> tinr -> hit_q and more loads on imem_ready, the head of the logged imem_ready -> ID path); after r14s2 this confirms that any u_fs change, stateless or not, costs more Fmax than any remaining fetch-side cycle bucket (all ≤ ~2%), so close the predictor/fetch-store front on this base, and do not build a change its own hypothesis rates below the 4.6% margin except in the same diff as the change it is meant to stack with.
